articles.title: 86 to 101: Virat Kohli's final ODI window to break Sachin Tendulkar's century record
articles.summary: It was the semi-final of the 2023 World Cup when Virat Kohli scored his 50th ODI century in front of Sachin Tendulkar, surpassing his idol's record of 49
articles.body: It was the semi-final of the 2023 World Cup when Virat Kohli scored his 50th ODI century in front of Sachin Tendulkar, surpassing his idol's record of 49 hundreds in the format. That innings put another Tendulkar record within Kohli's reach. Tendulkar's 100 international centuries remain the benchmark, leaving Kohli with a chance to become the first batter to reach 101.But the equation changed when Kohli retired from Test cricket on May 12, 2025. With his T20I career already over, ODI cricket became his only remaining route to Tendulkar's record. Now, with the 2027 World Cup less than a year away, Kohli has 86 international centuries - 14 short of equalling Tendulkar and 15 away from surpassing him.His latest hundred, a 139 not out against West Indies in the first ODI of the recently concluded series, was followed by 29 in the second match and a golden duck in the third.So how many opportunities does Kohli have left, and can he turn them into the 15 centuries he needs to move past Tendulkar's 100?86 to 101: The century equation beginsIndia currently have 11 confirmed bilateral ODIs scheduled before the 2027 World Cup - five against New Zealand, three against Sri Lanka and three against Zimbabwe. India's World Cup campaign will begin against Australia in Cape Town on October 7, 2027.The new FTP could add another six-match ODI series in South Africa in the weeks before the World Cup, giving India a chance to acclimatise to conditions ahead of the tournament. However, that series is not part of the confirmed schedule as of yet.The Asia Cup is another part of the picture. The 2027 tournament is scheduled to be played in Bangladesh from June 18 to July 4 and is expected to return to the ODI format. A detailed fixture list has not been announced, but based on the 2023 format, India could play up to six matches if they reach the final.The World Cup itself will have five group-stage matches and if the team reaches the Super 7, they will play six more matches, with a semi-final and final to follow if they go all the way. A finalist could therefore play a maximum of 13 matches at the tournament.That leaves Kohli with 11 confirmed bilateral ODIs before the World Cup, with the Asia Cup providing additional opportunities before the tournament.For Kohli, the target remains 15 centuries.India or overseas? The recent pattern in Kohli's centuriesKohli's recent ODI numbers are markedly different at home and overseas. In his last 32 ODI matches in India, he has scored nine centuries. In his last 32 overseas ODIs, he has scored three - in Dubai, Chattogram and Colombo.That split comes into focus with India scheduled to play five ODIs in New Zealand before the World Cup.Kohli's overall record overseas, though, is substantial. He has scored 27 of his 55 ODI centuries outside India. Bangladesh is his most productive overseas country, with six centuries, followed by Sri Lanka and Australia with five each. He has four in the West Indies, three in South Africa and one each in New Zealand, England, Zimbabwe and the UAE.Sri Lanka remains one of Kohli's most productive opponents. Kohli has scored 10 ODI centuries against Sri Lanka, his highest tally against any opponent. The three-match series in December will be played in India, with the ODIs scheduled for December 13, 16 and 19. Zimbabwe follow with three matches on January 3, 6 and 9.2027 World Cup: Kohli's final shot at Sachin's recordKohli's World Cup record gives him a strong base to build on. In 37 World Cup matches, he has scored 1,795 runs at an average of 59.83, with five centuries and 12 half-centuries.The 2023 edition was his most productive World Cup. He scored 765 runs, including three centuries and six half-centuries, and finished as the tournament's leading run-scorer. It was also the tournament in which he scored his 50th ODI century, moving past Tendulkar's record of 49.Only ODI cricket remainsKohli has already crossed 15000 ODI runs, becoming only the second batter after Tendulkar to reach the mark. He did so in his 303rd innings. With Test and T20I cricket behind him, every international century Kohli scores from here will come in ODIs. He has also said that the 2027 World Cup will be his last World Cup for India.Fifteen hundreds remain between Kohli and 101.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'We all have huge sympathy': Why England cricket ready to fund West Indies Test
articles.summary: The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) could step in financially if needed to ensure England’s women play a Test in the West Indies next spring.
articles.body: The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) could step in financially if needed to ensure England’s women play a Test in the West Indies next spring. The match is planned as part of a multi-format series and is considered important preparation for England’s 2027 Ashes campaign.Cricket West Indies (CWI) recently announced several cost-cutting measures, including reductions in player contracts. Earlier this year, it also cancelled a planned women’s Test against Australia, although the rest of that tour went ahead.There have been no talks about cancelling England’s Test, and the wider tour, which includes three T20s and three ODIs, is not currently under threat.Speaking to the BBC, ECB chair Richard Thompson said: "I hope not. That's not expected to be cancelled. I hope it will take place."He also said the ECB would "look at" providing financial help if CWI faced difficulties staging the match.Normally, the host cricket board pays the costs of hosting visiting teams. However, touring in the Caribbean can be expensive because players often need to travel between different islands. CWI said it has spent more than $80m on domestic air travel over the past 15 years.'It's very important for us'Thompson said the ECB wants the Test to happen because England need more red-ball cricket before the Ashes."We want that Test match to play out," said Thompson. "It's very important for us because our first women's match in the Ashes is the Headingley Test, so we need a good red-ball warm-up."We've got to be playing somewhere and we'd much prefer that to be the West Indies."England have played just one Test since their Ashes defeat in early 2025, losing to India at Lord’s. They have not faced West Indies in a women’s Test since 1979, while West Indies last played a Test in 2004.England will also hold a 10-day red-ball training camp in India in January as part of their Ashes preparations.Thompson added: "We all have a huge sympathy for the West Indies, we all want to see a successful West Indian nation. They have very unique challenges and I hope through the International Cricket Council and others we can find a way through this."Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'No one treats a human being like that': Ravi Shastri calls out Pakistan's treatment of jailed Imran Khan
articles.summary: Former India head coach Ravi Shastri has spoken out over the reported treatment of jailed former Pakistan captain Imran Khan, calling it “inhumane” and
articles.body: Former India head coach Ravi Shastri has spoken out over the reported treatment of jailed former Pakistan captain Imran Khan, calling it “inhumane” and saying no person should be treated that way.Reports cited in the story claim Khan’s health has worsened in jail, with only 15% vision remaining in his right eye.Shastri backs Imran on humanitarian groundsSpeaking to Republic World, Shastri said he was shocked by Khan’s situation and believed cricketers around the world would share his concerns."I'm not a politician. But just to see the way he's being treated today is shocking. You know, no one treats a human being like that. On humanitarian grounds, I don't think he deserves what he's getting. So I don't speak just for myself. I think there'll be a lot of cricketers around the globe who will be echoing the same sentiments," said Shastri.He also wished Khan good health and praised his achievements as a cricketer and captain, particularly his ability to guide young players."I just hope he's well and his health is good. Because what he gave to the game was something special. And my memories of him are just being an outstanding leader. You know, just a leader of men. The ability to motivate youngsters and then take them through. You said he came close at the age of 40, captain of the side, and he won the World Cup with a pretty young team," he added.'He doesn't deserve it'Shastri said Khan, who has been in jail since 2023, is one of Pakistan’s most recognisable figures worldwide and should receive better treatment."Hopefully. Hope he comes out and is treated better. He's been there for a long time. You could be out somewhere else, in the same position, because I don't understand the politics. But to sit in a cell there, he doesn't deserve it because he's the most recognised Pakistani face globally. Whether you like it or not, that's my view," said Shastri.He also remembered Khan as a great all-rounder and leader, saying the India-Pakistan rivalry was built on mutual respect."This man you're seeing there with me was an unbelievable cricketer. I mean, a great cricketer is an understatement. articles.title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi or Sanju Samson? India face selection dilemma ahead of first T20I against West Indies
articles.summary: LUCKNOW: Coming off the golden glow of their Asian Games triumph in Japan, India step into Tuesday’s fivematch T20I series opener against the West Indies
articles.body: LUCKNOW: Coming off the golden glow of their Asian Games triumph in Japan, India step into Tuesday’s fivematch T20I series opener against the West Indies at the Ekana Stadium here carrying momentum, silverware and an intriguing selection headache at the top of the order.While Abhishek Sharma’s explosive presence as a designated opener is virtually etched in ink, the suspense lies in who walks out alongside him. It is a clash of narratives: the breathtaking audacity of youth versus the hardened composure of experience.In one corner stands teen prodigy Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, whose fearless strokeplay has set pulses racing across the circuit. In the other is Sanju Samson, the seasoned campaigner whose heroics in India’s 2026 T20 World Cup triumph remains etched in cricketing folklore.Will head coach Gautam Gambhir lean into the romance of the next generation, or will he trust the calm authority of a proven match-winner?Bowling coach Morne Morkel acknowledged the delicate juggling act ahead of the first T20I. “I’m pretty sure Gautam will look to rotate him (Sooryavanshi). That is up to the selectors, and the coach and the captain, in terms of the playing level, or which playing level will be the best to win a game for India on our home soil. In terms of the starting X, he guys just came back from an Asian Games, so we’re going to see how everybody’s feeling after jet lag, after travelling, and then from there, make plans accordingly.”Fatigue, indeed, remains a tangible hurdle. “The red flag, or the problem, might be our guys travelling back and then immediately playing an international match after the Asian Games,” Morkel said. “Some of the guys arrived only a couple of days ago. But I think once we are up and running, and the series gets going, we will be up for it.”The spotlight will also be on skipper Shreyas Iyer. In his last 10 outings at the helm, a half-century has eluded him. Iyer’s blade yielded just 34 runs across two Asian Games fixtures and 48 in three matches against Afghanistan.Fortunately for India, their bowling arsenal welcomes back two electrifying local favourites returning to action after the Zimbabwe tour in July: Mayank Yadav and Prince Yadav.Standing in India’s way is a dangerous West Indies outfit marshalled by Shai Hope, who is in blistering touch following back-to-back ODI centuries.For the Caribbean side, Lucknow is a familiar venue. They spent nearly a month in the city in 2019 when Afghanistan used the Ekana Stadium as their home ground. Though history has rarely been kind to them, yielding just one win and three losses in four T20Is at the venue compared to India’s dominant 3-1 ledger.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India 'A' pacers look to step up to the plate against Australia 'A'
articles.summary: PUDUCHERRY: In an era where 350-plus totals in ODIs are becoming the norm, fast bowlers are often left walking a tightrope.
articles.body: PUDUCHERRY: In an era where 350-plus totals in ODIs are becoming the norm, fast bowlers are often left walking a tightrope. India’s recent ODI series against the West Indies was a case in point, with the bowlers conceding 295 and 405 in the first two games before West Indies chased down 352 in the final ODI with 10 balls to spare.As India look towards the 2027 World Cup, where they begin their campaign against Australia on Oct 7, the threematch one-day series between India ‘A’ and Australia ‘A’ in Puducherry offers another window into the country’s pace reserves.The big question is: who can eventually emerge as the ideal partner for Jasprit Bumrah?With Arshad Khan, Gurjapneet Singh and Yash Thakur are part of the India ‘A’ setup, it will be interesting to see if anyone can step up.India ‘A’ coach Lakshmipathy Balaji believes the cupboard is far from bare. For him, the answer lies as much in patience and nurturing as it does in raw numbers.“Many have potential. High-scoring games are common now, but bowlers will adapt over time. Bumrah became world-class through time, effort and experience. Youngsters like Anshul (Kamboj) and Gurnoor (Brar) need time and grooming to match international demands. It won’t always be 350-400 run games; bowlers will adapt to modern demands very soon,” Balaji said.Anshul Kamboj was handed his ODI debut in the third game against West Indies after Prasidh Krishna was ruled out. It was, however, a baptism of fire as he conceded 82 runs in nine overs. Gurnoor Brar, who has nine ODIs under his belt, also had an expensive series, while Auqib Nabi went for 84 in 8.5 overs on his ODI debut. Prasidh, too, had a difficult outing in his two games.Yet Balaji does not see the recent run-fests as a cause for concern.“Nothing is lacking, everyone is working hard. Since both teams have scored heavily, batting has temporarily moved ahead of bowling in modern cricket. Once bowling units click together, a balanced contest between bat and ball will return soon,” he said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Suryakumar Yadav left out of Mumbai Ranji Trophy squad despite availability: 'He needs more red-ball cricket'
articles.summary: MUMBAI: In another huge boost to his fledgling career and a vote of confidence in his abilities, Mumbai's senior selection committee, led by Rajesh Pawar,
articles.body: MUMBAI: In another huge boost to his fledgling career and a vote of confidence in his abilities, Mumbai's senior selection committee, led by Rajesh Pawar, on Monday appointed opener Ayush Mhatre as the new vice-captain of Mumbai’s Ranji Trophy squad for the first match of the 2026-27 season against Chandigarh from Oct 11 at the Wankhede Stadium, even as they snubbed India's 2026 T20 World Cup winning captain Suryakumar Yadav, who had earlier confirmed his availability and willingness to be a part of Mumbai's Ranji side, on the grounds that he needed to "play more red-ball cricket."The 16-member squad, which will be captained by veteran batter Siddhesh Lad, includes India's Test opener Yashasvi Jaiswal and Sarfaraz Khan.The 36-year-old Suryakumar didn't feature in any of pre-season tournaments for Mumbai, the local Kanga League, and didn't take part in the in Mumbai's intra-squad matches at the Brabourne Stadium and the MCA's ground in BKC recently."If Surya were to be picked, Musheer Khan, who scored 96 for West Zone in the Duleep Trophy in Aug, would have had to be dropped. That wasn't feasible," a source in the Mumbai Cricket Association told TOI.The selection committee was attended by former India skipper Dilip Vengsarkar, who is the MCA's Cricket Advisor."Surya is available but it was thought to go with the youngsters for the time being. He is obviously a big-match player and a proven performer for Mumbai. We just want to get into rhythm by playing a few red-ball matches. Surya hasn’t played a red-ball match for the last 18 months, so we want him to have a few games under his belt and then he can get into the team," Pawar told reporters.Throwing light on the appointment of Lad and Mhatre as the new captain and vice-captain of the Mumbai team, Pawar said, "The selection committee unanimously has gone with experienced Siddhesh Lad as the captain for the seasons. Along with a senior, we have planned to groom a junior in Ayush as the vice-captain. He has led the India Under-19 to the (U-19) World Cup win, is a smart cricketer and is in excellent nick."TOI had reported about veteran seam bowling allrounder Shardul Thakur suffering from a hand injury during a practice match at the Cricket Club of India after being struck by a ball hit by Mhatre and is likely to miss a few matches initially of Mumbai's 2026-27 Ranji Trophy campaign. "Shardul has a slight fracture in his right middle finger. He may be unavailable for the first two matches," Pawar said.Talking about Jaiswal being available for the first Ranji game, Pawar said, "It’s very good that Yashasvi is playing the season-opener. He also needs game-time and the team will also benefit. His availability and that of a lot of players for the next game is yet to be known due to the impending India and India A selection, so we have selected the squad only for the first game."Reposing his faith in the Mumbai squad picked for the first Ranji Trophy match, Pawar said, "The preparation has been excellent. We played four-day games at the KSCA Invitational and then played in Puducherry as well. We could properly watch 25 to 30 players in action and based on it, we have selected a squad that is ready for the season. This is our best team and the youngsters have also come in on the back of excellent performances and the seasoned players are in-form for India A and Duleep Trophy."A notable omission was young opener Angkrish Raghuvanshi, who recently scored a double century (203) for Rest of India Under-23 team against CK Nayudu Trophy champions Tamil Nadu on the weekend. "Angkrish has missed out over here but he will be involved in the U-23 squad," Pawar said.Mumbai’s Ranji Trophy Squad: Siddhesh Lad (C), Yashasvi Jaiswal, Ayush Mhatre (VC), Divyansh Saxena, Musheer Khan, Sarfaraz Khan, Suved Parkar, Aakash Anand (WK), Hardik Tamore (WK), Shams Mulani, Tanush Kotian, Atharva Ankolekar, Tushar Deshpande, Mohit Awasthi, Sylvester Dsouza, Onkar Tarmale.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Hardik Pandya's famous World Cup celebration returns, this time with MrBeast and CarryMinati
articles.summary: Hardik Pandya has brought back one of his most recognisable celebrations, but this time, he had two very different personalities alongside him.
articles.body: Hardik Pandya has brought back one of his most recognisable celebrations, but this time, he had two very different personalities alongside him. The India all-rounder joined hands with global YouTube star MrBeast and popular Indian creator CarryMinati to recreate his famous hands-out shrug celebration.MrBeast, whose real name is Jimmy Donaldson, is the most subscribed YouTube creator in the world. He became the first individual creator to cross 500 million subscribers earlier this year. CarryMinati, whose real name is Ajey Nagar, is among India’s biggest YouTubers.MrBeast shared the photograph as part of a collection from his recent India visit. The post also featured pictures from his meetings with several other celebrities, including Pandya."Had an amazing trip to India," Mr Beast captioned the photos.Pandya responded to the post, asking the YouTube star to return to India soon."My brother. Come visit us again soon." Pandya replied.The story behind Pandya’s iconic celebrationPandya made the shrug celebration famous after India won the 2024 T20 World Cup in Barbados. The gesture is similar to the shrug popularised by social media star Khaby Lame.Pandya played an important role in India’s victory over South Africa in the final. He bowled the decisive final over before celebrating the title with the now-famous pose.Pandya has played 11 Tests, 94 ODIs and 138 T20Is in his career so far.In 138 T20Is, Pandya has scored 2288 runs at an average of 28.24 and a strike rate of 145.91. articles.title: 'I feel I have done my duty': Harmanpreet Kaur steps down as India captain
articles.summary: India women’s long-serving captain Harmanpreet Kaur has stepped down from captaincy in all three formats.
articles.body: India women’s long-serving captain Harmanpreet Kaur has stepped down from captaincy in all three formats. The 37-year-old said she had fulfilled her responsibility as captain and is now ready to return to the game without the pressure of leading the side.“Today, I step down as captain of the Indian Women's Cricket Team across all formats,” she posted on her Instagram account.‘This is not an easy decision’Harmanpreet said giving up the captaincy was an emotional decision after years of leading India.“This is not an easy decision. It carries years of memories, emotions, sacrifices, and moments that will stay with me for the rest of my life,” Harmanpreet said in a lengthy statement.She also made it clear that stepping down as captain does not mean the end of her international career.“Now, I'm ready to play for the love of the game again. Captaincy ends. The journey continues,” she added.A decade as T20I captainHarmanpreet took charge of India’s T20I team in 2016 and remained in the role for 10 years. She became the ODI captain in 2022 before taking over as the all-format leader in 2023.Her time as captain included some of India women’s biggest achievements. Under her leadership, India won their maiden ODI World Cup in November last year and recently secured a second successive Asian Games gold in the T20 format.Harmanpreet said she was stepping away from leadership with confidence in the team’s future.“I’m leaving the captaincy with a heart full of emotions, but also with peace,” she said.“Because I genuinely believe my team is in a good place,” she said.HARMANPREET KAUR STATEMENT:Today, I step down as captain of the Indian Women’s Cricket Team across all formats.This is not an easy decision. It carries years of memories, emotions, sacrifices, and moments that will stay with me for the rest of my life.I have given everything I had to this team and to Indian women’s cricket — my blood, my sweat, my time, and many times, a part of my own game and personal ambitions. There were moments when I had to put my individual performance, my own growth, and what I wanted for myself aside, because I believed the team had to come first.As a captain, I have had to make difficult decisions.Decisions that were not always understood, not always easy, and sometimes came at a personal cost. But every decision I made was with one intention - to make this TEAM better and to give other players the opportunity to grow, believe in themselves and become the best versions of themselves.I have seen it all.I have seen the lowest moments, the heartbreak, the criticism, the doubts and the days when nothing seemed to go our way. And I have also experienced the highest highs - the victories, the celebrations, the pride of representing our country, and the moments that made every sacrifice worth it.| leave the captaincy today with a heart full of emotions , but also with PEACE .Because I genuinely believe My team is in a good place. A team with talent, character, belief and a future that I am incredibly excited to watch and be a part of .I feel I have done my duty.I gave this team everything I had. I carried the responsibility with pride, and I will always be grateful for the privilege of leading Indian women’s cricket.Now, it is time for me to turn the page.Captaincy may end today, but my love for Indian cricket never will.Thank you to every teammate, coach, support staff, management , BCCI , family members every single fan who stood by me through the highs and lows.Blood. Sweat. Sarifice. Pride.I gave it allNow, I’m ready to play for the love of the game again.Captaincy ends. articles.title: Prasidh Krishna likely to be out of action for three weeks; touch and go for New Zealand ODIs
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India pacer Prasidh Krishna is set to be out of action for at least three weeks and could be touch and go for the five-match ODI series against
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India pacer Prasidh Krishna is set to be out of action for at least three weeks and could be touch and go for the five-match ODI series against New Zealand, beginning November 4.Prasidh sustained a left hamstring injury during the second ODI against the West Indies in Guwahati and subsequently missed the third match of the series in New Chandigarh. He bowled just five overs in the Guwahati ODI before leaving the field in the 31st over of the West Indies innings. He picked up one wicket in the match and has three wickets from the two ODIs he has played in the series.The 30-year-old is also doubtful for the opening round of the Ranji Trophy, which begins on October 11. Karnataka will open their campaign against Andhra Pradesh in Vijayawada.It is learnt that Prasidh has checked into the BCCI's Centre of Excellence (CoE) in his hometown Bengaluru. He is expected to regain full fitness in around three weeks and could start bowling at full intensity in four weeks.His recovery timeline could make his availability for the New Zealand series a tricky proposition. Even if he returns to bowling by then, there is no guarantee that he will be ready to play from the start of the series. India could also be forced to manage their fast bowlers carefully, with Test-bound players expected to miss the last two ODIs against New Zealand.India captain Shubman Gill had admitted after the defeat in New Chandigarh that the absence of players due to injuries and scheduling issues had been frustrating.“I would say it’s been unfortunate, you know, with the injuries and with the scheduling with the other matches being around. It’s been a little bit unfortunate that we have not been able to play the bowling lineup that we would like to,” Gill told reporters.Gill is hopeful of having a full-strength squad available for the New Zealand ODIs, as India look to settle on their preferred combination ahead of the 2027 ODI World Cup.“I honestly think there is not that much time to experiment. The combination that we want to play, hopefully, we get all the players available from the next series. The combination that we would like to play in the World Cup, we want to start playing with that combination,” he said.Prasidh's fitness is therefore a significant concern for India. He is expected to be an important part of the team's plans for the New Zealand tour and the 2027 ODI World Cup in South Africa, Namibia and Zimbabwe. His injury adds to India's growing list of concerns ahead of an important phase in their preparations.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. The team finished on top in 2012, 2016, 2022 and 2026. She also led India to consecutive gold medals at the Asian Games. The team won gold in Hangzhou in 2022 before successfully defending the title at the Aichi-Nagoya Games in 2026.Harmanpreet also led India to their first bilateral women’s ODI series victory in England since 1999. India achieved the historic result in 2022. Her captaincy also produced major wins in the longer and shorter formats. articles.title: South Africa vs Australia Test series: 'Sandpapergate' adds to intrigue in rematch of infamous 2018 ball-fixing scandal
articles.summary: Shaun Pollock tells the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast: "I'm sure there'll be a few people coming dressed up in accordance with Sandpapergate.... But I don't think it'll be over the top or too intense"; watch the first Test, live on Sky Sports Cricket from 7.30am, Friday
articles.body:
The ball-tampering scandal that rocked cricket occurred during the Cape Town Test in March 2018 - a series South Africa would go on to win 3-1 - when Cameron Bancroft was shown on TV using a small, yellow object that ultimately proved to be a piece of sandpaper to tamper with the ball.

He was banned for nine months by Cricket Australia for his actions, with 12-month bans dished out to then captain Steve Smith and vice-captain David Warner for their part in proceedings and prior knowledge of the plan.

Reflecting on the incident more than six years on, former South Africa bowler Shaun Pollock told the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast : "I wasn't on air at the time, but I can remember when it came out and the major impact that it had.

"We were getting messages from back home of people going, 'I can't believe this has happened'.

"For the next hour or two, whatever happened on the cricket field was kind of irrelevant to everything that was going on. We knew there was trouble brewing."

Australia haven't toured South Africa since, with a proposed trip in early 2021 called off due to the pandemic.

But South Africa did claim a notable victory over Australia at Lord's last summer, winning the World Test Championship final , and Durban's series-opener on Friday serves as the team's first home Test in the 16 months since.

England visit for a three-Test tour of their own, starting in December. But Pollock believes it's Australia who will be the prized scalp.

"There's definitely something special about the Australia series," he said. "There's obviously some wonderful history between South Africa and England, and we'll thoroughly enjoy that series too - I know the Barmy Army are coming out - but I think it's Australia [if fans had to choose], to be brutally honest."

"The World Test Championship win has definitely created a bigger appetite for Test cricket in South Africa. That's been a real plus for us, and I'm sure the mace will be paraded around all the venues, considering it is Australia that we play."

Pollock added: "What will their reception be? I don't think it'll be overly hostile.

"The coverage over here, there's been quite a few replays of the [2018] series over the last few weeks, just to sort of create a bit of animosity, I suppose.

"But when you play against Australia, people in South Africa won't need a reason to, I don't know, write a billboard or have a go at them about some particular reason.

"I'm sure there'll be a few people coming dressed up in accordance with Sandpapergate. I'm sure there'll be some continual reminding of it. But I don't think it'll be over the top or too intense."

As for the series itself, Pollock is predicting 2-1 successes in both series, against Australia and England, pointing to the former's misfiring batting line-up as particular cause for optimism.

"Australia's batting would be a concern for me," he said. "I watched the one-day series and they didn't play spin that well at all, and that might even tempt South Africa to play two spinners in the first Test.

"And there's obviously a lot of talk in circles about should Marnus [Labuschagne] be there or should this guy be there? It's not settled.

"Think back to the days we played, there were guys queuing up for an opportunity, and they only got a chance where there was injury. Whereas now it's a case of kind of throwing all the balls up in the air.

"I just think they're very unsettled. They rely massively on Steve Smith and Travis Head, in particular."

Watch the first Test between South Africa and Australia live on Sky Sports Cricket from Friday (7.30am on air, 8.30am first ball).

articles.title: 'Captaincy ends': Harmanpreet Kaur’s top five achievements as India captain
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Harmanpreet Kaur’s decision to step down as captain of the Indian women’s cricket team across all three formats marks the end of one of the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Harmanpreet Kaur’s decision to step down as captain of the Indian women’s cricket team across all three formats marks the end of one of the longest and most significant leadership eras in Indian women’s cricket.The 37-year-old, who led India’s T20I side for a decade after taking over in 2016, became the ODI captain in 2022 before taking charge across formats in 2023. On Tuesday, she announced that she was ready to move on from leadership and return to playing simply “for the love of the game”.“Captaincy ends. The journey continues,” Harmanpreet wrote in her farewell statement.Her tenure was defined by landmark victories, records and moments that helped shape the modern era of Indian women’s cricket.From finally winning the ODI World Cup to establishing herself among the most successful captains in T20I history, Harmanpreet leaves behind a remarkable leadership legacy.Here are the five biggest achievements of Harmanpreet Kaur’s captaincy stint.1. Leading India to its maiden Women’s ODI World Cup titleThe biggest achievement of Harmanpreet Kaur’s captaincy was undoubtedly India’s historic triumph in the Women’s ODI World Cup in November 2025.For decades, an ODI World Cup title had remained one of the biggest missing pieces in Indian women’s cricket. India had come agonisingly close before, finishing runners-up in 2005 and 2017, but the trophy continued to elude the team.That changed under Harmanpreet.Leading India on home soil, she oversaw the campaign that finally delivered the country its first-ever Women’s ODI World Cup title. The achievement carried enormous significance not only for Harmanpreet personally but also for the growth and visibility of women’s cricket in India.The triumph represented the culmination of years of progress. India had developed into a consistent force in international cricket, producing a generation of players capable of competing with the world's best. Harmanpreet's leadership was central to that transition.Winning a World Cup as captain is the defining achievement of any international cricketer. For Harmanpreet, doing so with the Indian women's team made the moment even more significant.The title also ensured that her captaincy legacy would be remembered for more than individual records. She became the leader who helped India cross the final barrier and turn years of promise into a world championship.2. Leading India to back-to-back Asian Games gold medalsAnother significant achievement of Harmanpreet Kaur’s captaincy was leading India to gold medals at consecutive Asian Games, reinforcing the team’s dominance in the T20 format on the continental stage.India won the women’s cricket gold medal at the 2022 Asian Games in Hangzhou, where cricket made its return to the Games after a long absence. Harmanpreet’s side emerged victorious in the T20 competition, securing India’s first-ever Asian Games gold in women’s cricket.India then successfully defended its title at the 2026 Asian Games, once again finishing at the top of the women’s T20 competition. The back-to-back triumphs highlighted the consistency of the Indian team under Harmanpreet’s leadership and added another pair of major medals to her captaincy résumé.Winning one Asian Games gold was a landmark achievement. Repeating that success four years later demonstrated that India had established itself as the dominant force in the continental competition.3. Winning four Asia Cup titlesAnother defining feature of Harmanpreet's captaincy has been India's dominance in the continental game.Under her leadership, India secured four Asia Cup titles, in 2012, 2016, 2022 and 2026, giving Harmanpreet the distinction of being the Indian captain with the most Asia Cup triumphs.The Asia Cup has traditionally been an important tournament for women's cricket in the region, providing teams with an opportunity to test themselves against familiar opponents while also developing younger players.For India, success in the competition has reflected the team's sustained strength.Harmanpreet's four titles also demonstrate the longevity of her leadership. The fact that her successful campaigns stretched across more than a decade is particularly notable. Different teams, different opponents and different generations of Indian players came and went, but Harmanpreet remained a constant presence.The achievement saw her surpass Mithali Raj for the most Asia Cup titles by an Indian captain.That places Harmanpreet in distinguished company. Mithali was one of the central figures of Indian women's cricket for more than two decades, and succeeding her in the record books is a significant marker of Harmanpreet's own influence.The 2026 title was especially important because it came near the end of her captaincy tenure, providing another continental trophy to close one of the most successful leadership chapters in Indian women's cricket.4. Dominating T20I cricket and setting historic leadership milestonesHarmanpreet Kaur’s impact was perhaps most pronounced in T20I cricket, where she spent a decade at the helm after taking over as India’s captain in 2016. Her remarkable longevity not only made her one of the longest-serving leaders in women’s international cricket but also saw her establish several historic records.One of her biggest achievements came when she surpassed Australia’s Meg Lanning to become the captain with the most wins in women’s T20 internationals. The record reflects the consistency and longevity of Harmanpreet’s leadership at a time when the shortest format was undergoing rapid growth around the world.Her T20I tenure also produced another extraordinary milestone. Harmanpreet became the first cricketer in history to captain a side in 150 T20I matches, underlining the remarkable length of her leadership career.Reaching that landmark required far more than simply holding the captaincy. It reflected sustained selection, fitness, performance and, crucially, the confidence of teammates and coaches over many years. During her tenure, women's cricket witnessed the rise of franchise leagues, increasingly demanding international schedules and major tactical developments in T20 cricket.5. Leading India to a historic Test victory at Lord’sWhile Harmanpreet's greatest achievements have largely come in limited-overs cricket, one of her most memorable leadership moments arrived in the longest format.She guided India to a dominant 270-run victory over England at Lord's, in the first women's Test match played at the historic London venue.Lord's is one of the most iconic grounds in world cricket, and playing there carries enormous significance regardless of format. For the women's game, the occasion was historic in its own right.India's victory made the event even more memorable.A Test match places very different demands on a captain compared with T20 cricket. Leaders must manage sessions rather than individual overs, balance workloads across multiple days and constantly assess pitch conditions, field placements and bowling changes.Harmanpreet's ability to guide India to a comprehensive victory demonstrated her adaptability as a leader.The 270-run margin also highlighted India's superiority during the match. It was not merely a narrow escape or a hard-fought result; it was a commanding performance at one of cricket's most famous venues.For Harmanpreet, the achievement added another dimension to her captaincy record.A legacy that goes beyond the numbersHarmanpreet Kaur's decision to step down brings an era to a close, but her contribution to Indian women's cricket will extend far beyond captaincy statistics.She led India through a period of enormous change, from the rapid growth of T20 cricket to the expansion of women's franchise leagues and the eventual breakthrough of a World Cup triumph.Her five standout achievements, the 2025 ODI World Cup, the T20I captaincy wins record, four Asia Cup titles, the 150-match leadership milestone and the historic Lord's Test victory, encapsulate the scale of her tenure.Yet perhaps the most telling part of her farewell was her belief that the team is now “in a good place”.Harmanpreet is stepping away from the leadership role, but not from the game. As she put it, she is now ready to play for the love of cricket again.The captaincy may have ended. articles.title: Harmanpreet Kaur: India batter steps down as national team captain in all three formats
articles.summary: India batter Harmanpreet Kaur leaves her role as national team captain across all three formats of international cricket.
articles.body:
India batter Harmanpreet Kaur has left her role as national team captain across all three formats of international cricket.

Harmanpreet led India in five Tests, 51 one-day internationals and 155 T20 internationals and took her country to their first global title, winning the 50-over World Cup last year .

The 37-year old last captained her country on 22 September, when she helped secure a second successive Asian Games title against Sri Lanka.

In a post on Instagram , external , Harmanpreet said she was leaving the India side in a "good place" and that she's now "ready to play for the love of the game again".

"This is not an easy decision," Harmanpreet wrote. "It carries years of memories, emotions, sacrifices, and moments that will stay with me for the rest of my life.

"I have given everything I had to this team and to Indian women's cricket - my blood, my sweat, my time, and many times, a part of my own game and personal ambitions.

"There were moments when I had to put my individual performance, my own growth, and what I wanted for myself aside, because I believed the team had to come first.

"As a captain, I have had to make difficult decisions. Decisions that were not always understood, not always easy, and sometimes came at a personal cost. But every decision I made was with one intention - to make this TEAM better and to give other players the opportunity to grow, believe in themselves and become the best versions of themselves."

Harmanpreet, who first captained India in 2012, led her side to victory in the one-off Test against England at Lord's in July .

However India exited the T20 World Cup in the group stage earlier in the month, failing to reach the semi-finals for the second successive edition of the tournament.

Her announcement comes a day after Harmanpreet met with vice-captain Smriti Mandhana, head coach Amol Muzumdar and Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) secretary Devajit Saikia in Guwahati.

Mandhana, 30, is expected to takeover the captaincy, with India set to welcome Zimbabwe for three T20s and three ODIs from 16 October.

articles.title: ‘We’re not trying to be any other league’: SA20 COO Lynn Naudé on the league’s rapid rise
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Four seasons into its existence, SA20 has already established itself as one of the most prominent T20 leagues outside the IPL.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Four seasons into its existence, SA20 has already established itself as one of the most prominent T20 leagues outside the IPL. But for COO Lynn Naudé, the league’s rapid rise has been less about chasing quick wins and more about getting the fundamentals right. From securing a prime South African summer window and putting Proteas at the heart of the competition to creating a strong match-day atmosphere, Naudé explains how SA20 has built its identity and what lies ahead in Season 5.ExcerptsSA20 has grown rapidly in four seasons. What has been the biggest lesson behind that success?I think probably the biggest lesson is that strong foundations matter more than quick wins. From the very start, we were very single-minded about what we believed success looked like. The fan experience, the quality of cricket and putting South African players at the heart of the competition were all important to us. We wanted to make sure SA20 felt like it belonged to South African fans as a starting point, and then we could take it global from there.I think that's probably been one of my biggest learnings. If you can get your basics right, the rest will follow from thereHow do you keep SA20 distinct in an increasingly crowded global T20 calendar?T20 cricket has got a unique feeling to it, and that's possibly a common thread. But I think there are a couple of things that have helped us.First, our window and our ability to secure it in the heart of the South African summer, with great conditions and full stadiums, was a real coup for us. That time of year lends itself to delivering a product that speaks very much to the fans, but also provides a fantastic experience both on broadcast and in the stadium.The second is the quality of the competition. The commitment from Cricket South Africa to make all of its Proteas available to play in the tournament season after season, and to see them compete with the best in the world, means that we have intentionally put cricket at the heart of the product.The third is probably the atmosphere at the venues. I think that's become something quite synonymous with SA20.If I had to wrap it up, I'd say we're not trying to be any other league. We're just trying to be the best version of SA20 that we can be.”What role has the league played in strengthening South African cricket beyond the professional level?It has actually been on multiple levels. The intention was for SA20 to almost become a bastion for South African cricket. There was obviously work that needed to be done to strengthen the talent pipeline.But outside of that, if I look back again on the last five seasons, it's also about the quality of the broadcast, what's improved in terms of the fan experience within the South African sporting context, our venues, the ways of working and how they operate on a day-to-day basis.There's also been a lot of knowledge transfer from SA20 into the greater cricket ecosystem, with some of the standards and expectations that we have for the type of product we want to deliver.We've had the opportunity to expose a lot of young talent in the sporting industry to our ways of working and the culture at SA20.In the lead-up to the 2027 World Cup, what we've tried to do is make sure that the cricket ecosystem, and those who deliver not only on the field but also off it, is better off the back of SA20 and the experience it has brought to the South African cricket landscape.With overseas leagues expanding, how do you ensure SA20 continues attracting elite international players?At the highest level, elite players want to play where the cricket is competitive, the conditions are good and the environment is professional. I think that's something we strive to offer, and I think we do offer all three.Our franchises bring global experience and know how to run teams. The players know that when they come here, they'll be tested against strong domestic talent and they'll be playing in front of full stadiums.It's always surprising to me, anecdotally, when I hear players talk about how important it is to them to play in front of a crowd and how different it feels. I guess when you're talented like that, you feel appreciated when you're playing in front of a lot of people.That, coupled with the strong and stable franchise ownership groups that we've got, who invest in those players, offers them opportunities.If you have the opportunity to play in the SA20, you also have the opportunity to play in many other places around the world. I think consistency across all of those things will make sure that we remain attractive to players.Looking ahead to Season 5, what is the one area where you want fans to notice a clear step forward?Every season we run a fan survey, and it directly shapes what we deliver. Our fans have told us what they want to see more of, and they've also told us what they don't want us to change. Those are the types of things that shape our decisions.Our brand positioning at SA20 is ‘for everyone’, and we take that pretty seriously. On the field, it means competitive, world-class cricket for the dedicated cricket fan. Off the field, it really means a great social occasion for people to come and enjoy the atmosphere, the music and a day out with friends and family.If I have to say what I want fans to take away, it's that we do hear you, we do listen to what you want, and we will always strive to deliver based on the feedback that fans are giving us.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Harmanpreet Kaur: India's World Cup-winning captain steps down from role across all three formats of cricket
articles.summary: Harmanpreet Kaur led India to first-ever global women's cricket title on home soil in 2025 as they beat South Africa in the 50-over World Cup final;  batter, 37, says she has given "everything" to India while captaining in five Tests, 51 one-day internationals and 155 T20 internationals
articles.body:
The batter, 37, led India to their first-ever global women's title at the 2025 50-over World Cup on home soil.

Harmanpreet is only the third Indian captain, after men's players Kapil Dev and MS Dhoni, to guide a team to victory in that event.

Her last act in charge was steering her country to a second straight Asian Games gold last month, with India thrashing Sri Lanka by 147 runs in the final.

Overall, Harmanpreet - who is likely to be succeeded by Smriti Mandhana - captained in five Tests, 51 one-day internationals and 155 T20 internationals.

'I have given everything I had to this team'

Writing on Instagram, Harmanpreet said: "This is not an easy decision. It carries years of memories, emotions, sacrifices, and moments that will stay with me for the rest of my life.

"I have given everything I had to this team and to Indian women's cricket - my blood, my sweat, my time, and many times, a part of my own game and personal ambitions.

"There were moments when I had to put my individual performance, my own growth, and what I wanted for myself aside, because I believed the team had to come first.

"As a captain, I have had to make difficult decisions. Decisions that were not always understood, not always easy, and sometimes came at a personal cost.

"But every decision I made was with one intention - to make this team better and to give other players the opportunity to grow, believe in themselves and become the best versions of themselves.

"I leave the captaincy with a heart full of emotions but also with peace. Because I genuinely believe my team is in a good place. A team with talent, character, belief and a future that I am incredibly excited to watch and be a part of.

"I feel I have done my duty. I gave this team everything I had. I carried the responsibility with pride, and I will always be grateful for the privilege of leading Indian women's cricket."

Harmanpreet's final Test as captain was the 270-run drubbing of England at Lord's in July, the first women's Test to be held at the ground.

She became T20 captain in 2016 and added the Test and ODI roles when Mithali Raj retired in 2022.

Harmanpreet added: "Captaincy may end today, but my love for Indian cricket never will.

"Blood. Sweat. Sacrifice. Pride. I gave it all. Now, I'm ready to play for the love of the game again. Captaincy ends. The journey continues."

India will host Zimbabwe for three T20 internationals and as many ODIs from October 16 before a tour of South Africa in December that is live on Sky Sports .

Dhruv Jurel and Kumar Kushagra could consequently get opportunities in the A matches. Rishabh Pant, who is currently being considered primarily for Tests, is expected to play at least one India A fixture as part of his preparations. KL Rahul, Devdutt Padikkal and Sai Sudharsan are also expected to feature in at least one A game. Rahul's schedule is particularly interesting as he is likely to be part of the ODI squad and could play the October 24 A fixture before joining the team in Auckland..India squad announcement live: Bumrah workload remains a dilemma Jasprit Bumrah's workload is another major issue confronting the selectors. As TimesofIndia.com first reported, the management wants the premier fast bowler to increase his workload before he joins the squad for the Wellington Test. One option is to have Bumrah play an India A fixture, but that could weaken the senior ODI attack, particularly if the Test regulars are already being managed across formats. A Ranji Trophy appearance had also been discussed as an alternative, although some decision-makers are understood to be uncomfortable with asking Bumrah to put in a heavy domestic workload immediately before an overseas Test assignment. The Ojha-led panel will therefore have to find a balance between preparation and workload management..India vs New Zealand 2026: Akash Deep and Mukesh in A plans Mukesh Kumar has returned to the selectors' radar after an impressive performance in the Irani Cup fixture against Jammu & Kashmir and is likely to be drafted into the India A squad for the three matches. Akash Deep is also expected to feature in the A series as he continues his comeback and builds towards the two Tests in New Zealand. The fast bowler missed a significant period because of injury and the selectors want him to be fully match-ready before the Test assignment. His workload in the A games could therefore be carefully monitored. Mukesh, meanwhile, could provide India with additional pace-bowling depth across the A and senior squads, depending on how the selections pan out..India squad announcement live: Red-ball exposure a priority TimesofIndia.com understands that giving Test regulars meaningful red-ball exposure ahead of the two Tests will be one of the selection committee's top priorities. The selectors do not want to dilute the senior limited-overs squads, but the overlap with the India A series provides an opportunity for Test players to get valuable match practice. Some India A bowlers could also be asked to stay back in New Zealand after completing their A-series assignments to assist the Test squad with preparations. During the previous tour of Sri Lanka, spinners Harsh Dubey, Tanush Kotian, Vipraj Nigam and Shivang Kumar had accompanied the Test squad. This time, fast bowlers could be given a similar role..India vs New Zealand 2026: Test preparation to drive selection The India men's senior selection committee is likely to convene either on Tuesday or Wednesday to finalise the four squads for the upcoming New Zealand tour, with interim chief selector Pragyan Ojha set to chair the meeting. The session was postponed from Monday as the selectors awaited Prasidh Krishna's fitness reports. The panel will pick the T20I, ODI, Test and India A squads for a tour that begins with the T20I series on October 22. However, the biggest challenge will be balancing the availability of players across the different formats. The India A series begins on October 24 and overlaps with both the T20Is and ODIs, making player management a key part of the selection discussions..India squad announcement live: Bigger Test squad planned for New Zealand A larger Test squad would give India additional cover during a demanding overseas tour, particularly because flying in replacements to New Zealand at short notice can be difficult. The BCCI has therefore taken a broader logistical approach to the tour and has reportedly prepared visas for around 60 top national cricketers. The pool will cover the T20I, ODI and Test squads as well as the India A contingent for the three unofficial red-ball matches. With Akash Deep now back to full fitness and showing his pace in domestic cricket, his Test recall could provide India with another fast-bowling option for the WTC assignments..India vs New Zealand 2026: Iyer could captain India in final two ODIs There is also a possibility that Gill and some of the Test regulars could be rested from the final two ODIs to allow them additional preparation time ahead of the Test series. If Gill opts to focus on Test preparation, vice-captain Shreyas Iyer could take over as captain for those matches. The Test squad itself could comprise 16 or 17 players, with the selectors considering an additional fast bowler given the demands of the New Zealand tour. Bumrah, Siraj, Prasidh, Brar and Akash Deep are currently in the mix, while Auqib Nabi, Mukesh Kumar and Anshul Kamboj are competing for a potential sixth pace-bowling slot. All three are also in line for India A selection..India squad announcement live: India A games to give Test specialists match time The overlap between the India A Tests and the first three ODIs could force the selectors and team management to carefully divide players between the two assignments. The first three ODIs are scheduled for November 4, 7 and 10, coinciding with the India A red-ball matches. Some players who are part of both plans may therefore miss the A Tests and instead play the ODIs. However, Test specialists and one-format players are expected to use the A series to build red-ball rhythm. Rishabh Pant, who is likely to be the first-choice Test wicketkeeper, Dhruv Jurel, Devdutt Padikkal and reserve opener Sai Sudharsan could feature in at least one of the three unofficial Tests..India vs New Zealand 2026: ODI-Test overlap creates selection dilemma The biggest challenge for the selectors will be managing the ODI and Test squads, with only four days separating the final ODI and the opening Test. The last ODI is scheduled for November 15 in Tauranga, while the first Test begins in Wellington on November 19. With one day likely to be consumed by travel, the players involved in both formats will have only around three days to train before the Test series begins. As many as seven or eight players could be involved in both squads, including captain Shubman Gill, Yashasvi Jaiswal, who is expected to be the reserve opener in the ODIs, KL Rahul, Jasprit Bumrah, Mohammed Siraj and Nitish Kumar Reddy. Prasidh Krishna and Gurnoor Brar are also in contention, subject to fitness..India squad announcement live: Three squads to be picked for New Zealand tour The four-member selection committee headed by Pragyan Ojha will have a busy meeting, with squads for the T20Is, ODIs and Tests to be picked alongside the India A squad for the shadow tour of New Zealand. India A are scheduled to play three unofficial Tests between October 24 and November 10 as preparation for the two World Test Championship matches. The senior side will also play five ODIs, which will serve as an important part of India's preparations for next year's 50-over World Cup. The T20I squad is expected to be the least complicated selection, with several members of the Asian Games gold-medal winning side and players currently involved in the West Indies series likely to retain their places..India vs New Zealand 2026: ‘Bowling at 138-140 kmph’ eases fitness concerns Akash's return was managed carefully, with the Indian team management specifically asking the Rest of India coaching staff to handle the pacer with caution. “The Indian team management had told Rest of India coaching staff that Akash Deep should be handled with care as he is due for national comeback for the New Zealand series,” a BCCI official privy to developments told PTI. The official also said Akash has returned fully fit and is bowling at his usual pace. “He is completely fit and bowling at an average speed of 138 to 140 kmph which is an indicator that all is well,” the official said. The selectors are expected to meet on Tuesday or Wednesday to finalise the squads..India squad announcement live: Akash Deep in line for Test recall Fast bowler Akash Deep is set for a Test recall as the selectors prepare to pick three India squads for the upcoming New Zealand tour, which begins with the T20I series on October 22. The 29-year-old pacer was out of action for seven months due to a lower-back stress injury but made a successful return to competitive cricket in the Irani Cup. Representing Rest of India, Akash picked up six wickets for 68 runs across two innings, bowling nearly 24 overs. His comeback has strengthened his case for a place in the Test squad, with the team management closely monitoring his workload and fitness..India vs New Zealand 2026: India squad announcement soon Hello and welcome to the live coverage of the India squad announcement for the upcoming New Zealand series. India will be playing all three formats in the tour.

articles.title: Asian Games gold medalist Abhishek Sharma, Shafali Verma among 4 Indians nominated for ICC Player of the Month awards
articles.summary: India’s dominant run in international cricket has earned four of its stars a place on the ICC Player of the Month shortlists for September, with Shubman
articles.body: India’s dominant run in international cricket has earned four of its stars a place on the ICC Player of the Month shortlists for September, with Shubman Gill and Abhishek Sharma nominated in the men’s category, while Shafali Verma and Shree Charani feature among the women’s nominees.Gill is in contention for a record-equalling fifth ICC Player of the Month award, while Abhishek has been shortlisted after producing one of the most explosive T20I innings of the month.Zimbabwe captain Sikandar Raza is the other nominee in the men’s category, while Sri Lanka captain Chamari Athapaththu joins Shafali and Charani on the women’s shortlist.Gill eyes fifth Player of the Month awardGill enjoyed a sensational September in ODIs against the West Indies, scoring 333 runs in two matches. The India captain began the series with a century in Thiruvananthapuram, scoring 110 in the opening ODI.He then produced a breathtaking 223 off just 133 balls, registering the fastest ODI double-century and powering India to a successful chase of 406 with eight wickets and 39 balls to spare. Gill's latest nomination gives him another chance to add to his ICC Player of the Month collection.Abhishek sets new T20I recordAbhishek Sharma was equally destructive in the shortest format, smashing 229 runs in four T20Is during September. His standout performance came against Afghanistan, when he smashed a stunning 108 off 34 balls, including a record-breaking 30-ball century.The knock made him the fastest Indian to score a T20I century, surpassing Rohit Sharma's previous mark of 35 balls. Abhishek, who won the ICC Player of the Month award in September last year, will now look to claim the honour again.Shafali leads India's Asia Cup chargeShafali Verma's explosive batting earned her a place on the women's shortlist after a prolific month across formats. The opener accumulated 360 runs at a strike rate of 184.61 and finished as the leading run-scorer in India's successful Women's Asia Cup campaign.She also contributed with the ball, picking up six wickets during the period. At the Asian Games, Shafali continued her impressive run, smashing an unbeaten 100 against Bangladesh in the semi-final before scoring 48 in the gold-medal match against Sri Lanka.Charani breaks ICC rankings recordShree Charani's outstanding September has also earned her recognition. The spinner claimed 18 wickets in seven T20Is at an impressive economy rate of 3.30. Her best moment came in the Asian Games final, where she returned figures of 2/13 to help India secure the gold medal. The performance took Charani to 817 rating points, the highest ever recorded in the ICC Women's T20I bowling rankings.Raza, Athapaththu complete the shortlistsZimbabwe captain Sikandar Raza earned his nomination after emerging as the leading run-scorer in his team's home ODI series against Australia. The recovery came through Shai Hope and Sherfane Rutherford, and things were looking good for the tourists at the halfway mark. Ideally, though, the visitors would have wanted him to bat through, which could have given them a chance to get close to 190.. articles.title: 'You gave Indian cricket everything': Yuvraj, Shafali, Dhawan pay tribute after Harmanpreet Kaur steps down as captain
articles.summary: Harmanpreet Kaur may have stepped away from captaincy, but her impact on Indian women’s cricket was impossible to miss as tributes poured in from across
articles.body: Harmanpreet Kaur may have stepped away from captaincy, but her impact on Indian women’s cricket was impossible to miss as tributes poured in from across the cricket fraternity on Tuesday.India’s only women’s World Cup-winning captain announced her decision to step down as skipper across all three formats, bringing an end to a leadership tenure that saw India lift their maiden Women’s World Cup title and win Asian Games gold.Among those to pay tribute were former India all-rounder Yuvraj Singh, current opener Shafali Verma and former India opener Shikhar Dhawan, who took to Instagram to acknowledge Harmanpreet’s contribution.‘You gave Indian cricket everything’: YuvrajYuvraj, who like Harmanpreet hails from Punjab, shared a picture of the 37-year-old holding the 2025 Women’s World Cup trophy.“You gave Indian cricket everything as captain, Harman. The responsibility, the pressure, the highs and the lows, you carried it all with pride. Well done for everything you've done for the team and for the nation,” Yuvraj wrote.Shafali recalls Harmanpreet’s supportShafali, who made her India debut under Harmanpreet’s leadership, shared a more personal message for her former captain.“Since the day I made my debut, you've always been there for me, on and off the field. From guiding me through the early days to standing by me through everything, I've always known I could count on you, Harman di, your contribution to Indian women's cricket is something that will always be remembered. You've led us through some incredible moments and helped shape the team we are today. Thank you for everything, captain,” Shafali wrote.Dhawan hails Harmanpreet’s legacyFormer India opener Shikhar Dhawan also joined the tributes, highlighting the impact Harmanpreet has had on Indian cricket.“Leadership is never just about the title, it’s about the impact you leave behind. Harmanpreet, you’ve given Indian cricket a lot to be proud of. Wishing you the best for everything ahead!” Dhawan posted on Instagram.Harmanpreet steps down after historic runHarmanpreet’s decision came after a BCCI review meeting in Guwahati to assess the women’s team’s recent trajectory. The meeting was chaired by BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia and attended by Harmanpreet, vice-captain Smriti Mandhana and head coach Amol Muzumdar. Harmanpreet said she had done her duty as captain and was now ready to “play for the love of the game again.” She will continue to represent India as a player.Harmanpreet leaves the leadership role having overseen two landmark achievements: India’s first Women’s World Cup title in November 2025 and Asian Games gold last month.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Paul Farbrace: Sussex boss leaves to become Lancashire director of cricket
articles.summary: Lancashire appoint Paul Farbrace as their new director of cricket weeks before he was due to begin the same role at Sussex.
articles.body:
Lancashire have appointed Sussex head coach Paul Farbrace as their new director of cricket, weeks before he was due to assume the same role at Hove.

Sussex confirmed in July that Farbrace, 59, would switch roles from head coach to director of cricket from November, where he would work on a part-time basis.

But he now departs to take over from Mark Chilton, who left the post at Old Trafford last month after five years in the job.

Lancashire finished the season seventh in Division Two of the County Championship, the lowest position in the club's history.

Meanwhile, Farbrace helped guide Sussex to third place in Division One, despite beginning the season with a 12-point penalty.

Lancashire director of cricket Chilton to leave

Farbrace to take up director role at Sussex

The financial problems at Hove which triggered that deduction led Farbace to announce in April that he would step down as head coach at the end of the 2026 season.

In July, he said he would be staying to move into a part-time director of cricket role and oversaw the appointment of Matt Walker as his successor as head coach.

However, the former England assistant coach - who led Sussex to promotion from Division Two in 2023 - has now opted to move to Lancashire.

"It is with mixed emotions that I am leaving Sussex after four years," Farbrace told the club's website , external .

"I will always be grateful to Sussex for giving me the honour of being head coach and allowing me to work with a fabulous group of players and staff."

articles.body: Naman Dhir makes his T20I debut against West Indies in the opening game of the five-match series, while teenage sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has been left out of India’s playing XI in Lucknow.Dhir, who made his ODI debut on September 27, received his maiden T20I cap from Arshdeep Singh ahead of the match. The youngster is still waiting to make his India debut on home soil.Captain Shreyas Iyer confirmed that India have opted to bowl first, with dew expected to come into play later in the evening.“We are going to bowl first. It's a mixed soil. There will be some dew as well. Travel was pretty hectic. Came last night, today we have turned up for the game but we are in the zone,” Iyer said at the toss.He also praised the West Indies' T20 pedigree, adding that the visitors have “brilliant batting and all-rounders.”Hope: West Indies wanted to bowl firstWest Indies captain Shai Hope said his side would also have preferred to chase, particularly with dew likely to make conditions easier for the batting side later in the game.“In India, it's usually a lot better to chase, especially due to dew coming into play,” Hope said.He stressed the importance of adapting quickly to different conditions and said West Indies would rely on their experienced players to support the younger members of the squad.Five changes for IndiaIndia have made five changes from the Asian Games squad. articles.title: India vs Pakistan clash fuels ODI World Cup 2027 ticket frenzy as demand crosses 1.1 million
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: More than 1.1 million ticket applications have already been submitted for the 2027 ODI World Cup, with the India-Pakistan clash emerging as the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: More than 1.1 million ticket applications have already been submitted for the 2027 ODI World Cup, with the India-Pakistan clash emerging as the biggest draw just days after the ballot opened on October 1, while India's other marquee fixtures are also generating extraordinary demand.More than 320,000 fans have registered for the ticket ballot since it opened, with applications pouring in for matches across South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia. The ballot will remain open until 23:59 CAT on November 21, giving supporters around the world more time to enter the draw.India-Pakistan clash leads massive ticket rushThe October 10 India-Pakistan group-stage clash in Johannesburg has attracted more than 110,000 ticket applications, making it the most sought-after fixture of the tournament so far. The two sides are in Group A alongside Australia, Afghanistan, Zimbabwe and Qualifier A.But the demand is not limited to the traditional India-Pakistan rivalry. The India-South Africa fixture has already received more than 92,000 applications, while India's meeting with Australia has attracted over 86,000.That means India's first three major group-stage fixtures occupy the top three spots in terms of ticket demand, underlining the enormous following for Shubman Gill's side even before the tournament gets underway.India will open their campaign against defending champions Australia in Cape Town on October 7, before facing Pakistan three days later in Johannesburg. The South Africa fixture is also among the most anticipated matches of the tournament, giving the hosts a major attraction against one of the sport's biggest fan bases.India feature in all four most in-demand fixturesIndia's popularity is further underlined by the demand for the pre-seeded Super 7 fixture against Pakistan on November 7. That match has already received almost 78,000 applications, making it the fourth most sought-after fixture at this stage.The November 21 final has also attracted close to 69,000 applications, highlighting the appetite for the tournament's biggest matches even before the group stage begins.The ballot's overwhelming early response has given organisers a clear indication of the global interest in the tournament, which will be staged across three southern African nations.ICC CEO Sanjog Gupta said the initial figures reflected the stature of the event and its growing global reach.“One million ticket applications in just over 48 hours of opening the ticket ballot is a demonstration of the attention, stature and affiliation for ICC Cricket World Cup 2027,” Gupta said.“ICC events are now spectacles which transcend cultural and geographic boundaries and serve as platforms to widen and deepen fandom for the sport.”Africa prepares for World Cup returnThe 2027 tournament will mark the return of a major ICC men's event to Africa after two decades, with South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia sharing hosting duties. The competition begins with the three-team Super Series in Namibia on October 2, before the group stage gets underway on October 7. The final is scheduled for Johannesburg on November 21.Gupta said the tournament would also provide an opportunity to expand cricket's reach across the continent.“This is also Africa’s moment to shine as an ICC marquee men’s event is returning to the continent after two decades and brings with it the attention of 2.5 billion cricket fans across 120+ countries,” he said.Qondisa Ngwenya, CEO of the 2027 World Cup Local Organising Committee, said the early ticket response was a “major statement by global fans” and showed the appetite to experience the tournament in southern Africa.With more than 1.1 million ticket applications already submitted and the ballot still open for several weeks, organisers can expect the numbers to climb further as anticipation builds for a World Cup featuring India-Pakistan, India-Australia and India-South Africa among its biggest early attractions.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
