articles.title: ‘Special place in Indian cricket history’: BCCI hails Harmanpreet Kaur after stepping down as India captain
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Harmanpreet Kaur’s 2025 Women’s World Cup triumph will remain the defining achievement of her captaincy and ensure that her contribution to
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Harmanpreet Kaur’s 2025 Women’s World Cup triumph will remain the defining achievement of her captaincy and ensure that her contribution to Indian cricket occupies a “special place” in its history, the BCCI said on Tuesday after the veteran batter stepped down as India’s leader across formats.BCCI president Mithun Manhas paid tribute to Harmanpreet’s leadership during a significant period of growth for women’s cricket in India, while expressing satisfaction that the 37-year-old will continue to represent the country as a player.“Harmanpreet Kaur's contribution as captain will always hold a special place in the history of Indian cricket,” Manhas said in a statement issued by the BCCI.“The World Cup victory in 2025 will undoubtedly be the defining achievement of her captaincy. It was the culmination of years of progress, hard work and belief. Her Asian Games gold medals and the many important victories during her tenure further underline the contribution she has made.”From World Cup triumph to a new chapterHarmanpreet took over India’s T20I captaincy in 2016 before becoming the full-time ODI and Test skipper in 2022 following Mithali Raj’s retirement. Her leadership stint culminated with India winning their maiden Women’s World Cup title in 2025 and successfully defending their Asian Games gold in Nagoya, Japan, last month.In her communication to the BCCI, Harmanpreet said she believed the time was right to hand over the captaincy but made it clear that her commitment to Indian cricket remained unchanged.“Leading India has been one of the greatest honours and privileges of my life,” she said.“After careful consideration, I believe that this is the right time for me to hand over the responsibility of captaincy and allow the team to move forward under new leadership.”The former captain also confirmed that she intends to continue playing for India and contribute to the team in a different capacity.“However, my commitment to Indian cricket remains as strong as ever. I would like to continue representing the Indian Women's Cricket Team as a player and contribute to the team's success in every way I can,” she said.A captaincy defined by historic milestonesHarmanpreet’s crowning achievement came in the 2025 World Cup final in Navi Mumbai, where India defeated South Africa by 52 runs to win their first ODI World Cup title.She had also played a pivotal role in the semifinal against Australia, scoring 89 and sharing a match-winning 167-run partnership with Jemimah Rodrigues as India chased down a record 339.Her leadership journey began more than a decade earlier. She first captained India in the 2012 Women’s T20 Asia Cup final against Pakistan after Mithali Raj and Jhulan Goswami were ruled out through injury, guiding the side to an 18-run victory and the inaugural title.She became India’s regular T20I captain in 2016 and assumed the ODI and Test captaincy after Mithali’s retirement. Under her leadership, India reached the 2020 Women’s T20 World Cup final, won silver at the 2022 Commonwealth Games and claimed their first Asian Games gold that year before successfully defending the title in Nagoya.Harmanpreet’s longevity has also produced a series of individual milestones. This year, she became the most-capped international player in women’s cricket, while also becoming the first player to feature in 200 T20Is and the first to captain in 150 T20Is.Long before becoming India’s all-format captain, she had established herself as one of the country’s biggest match-winners, most famously smashing an unbeaten 171 against Australia in the 2017 Women’s World Cup semifinal.BCCI backs Harmanpreet’s decision to continue playingBCCI secretary Devajit Saikia said Harmanpreet could be “immensely proud” of what she achieved as captain, particularly the journey that eventually culminated in the World Cup triumph.“You experienced the disappointment of falling short, but continued to believe in the team and its ability to achieve more. That is what made the World Cup victory in 2025 so special,” Saikia said.“You had been part of the journey for many years and eventually had the opportunity to lead India to its first Women's Cricket World Cup title. That will always remain one of the great moments in Indian cricket.”Saikia also praised the thought behind Harmanpreet’s decision to step aside while continuing as a player, saying her experience and influence would remain valuable to the younger members of the side.“I also appreciate the thought and consideration with which you have taken this decision. You have chosen to hand over the responsibility at a time when you believe the team is ready for a new chapter, while continuing to contribute as a player,” he said.Harmanpreet, meanwhile, said she was looking forward to remaining part of the India setup and supporting the team’s new leadership.“I look forward to continuing this journey in the India jersey and contributing to Indian cricket with the same pride, humility and commitment that I have always carried,” she said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: All-veg on matchday: Holkar stadium to serve up fasting-friendly platter on Navratri T20I clash
articles.summary: Holkar Stadium, Indore to offer all-vegetarian, Navratri fasting-friendly food for Oct 11 India vs West Indies T20I; non-veg only in hospitality.
articles.body: Indore: If you are a stickler for tempering your food or eating habits during the Navratras, then Indore’s Holkar stadium has a specially curated all-vegetarian platter ready to indulge your taste buds on October 11. The third India-West Indies T20I clash at Holkar stadium, which coincides with the beginning of the Navratri festival, will see the spectators filling the stands being served a vegetarian-only spread.Madhya Pradesh Cricket Association (MPCA), which is hosting the much-anticipated international fixture, has made special arrangements for spectators who will be observing fasts, adding faryali options to the match-day menu. Fans can also opt for sabudana mixture and plain or salted peanuts, allowing those observing the Navratri fast to have something to munch while enjoying the live cricket action on the field.For spectators not keeping a Navratri fast, the menu will feature a mix of familiar stadium snacks and more substantial vegetarian options. The menu chart features a lip-smacking range: veg pizzas, burgers, momos, sandwiches, vada pav, baked samosas, dal kachori, popcorn and paneer tikka. Beverage options include tea, coffee, ice cream, cream rolls, and soft drinks. Bottled water will also be served.Prices will range from Rs 10 for a 200-ml bottle of packaged water to Rs 250 for some of the paneer-based options. A 100-ml tea will cost Rs 20, while coffee will be available for Rs 30. Pizzas and Subway’s Veggie Delight will be priced at Rs 200.“The match day, Oct 11, coincides with the beginning of the Navratras. We have kept vegetarian-only stalls for spectators in the stands. Considering the many who will be keeping a fast on that day, faryali fasting options have also been included in the menu,” MPCA secretary Sudhir Asnani told TOI.The vegetarian menu, however, will apply only to the public areas of the stadium. Players and spectators in the hospitality area will have both vegetarian and non-vegetarian options to choose from.“Players and the spectators in the hospitality area will be served both veg and non-veg food as per their preference,” Asnani added.As international cricket returns to Holkar stadium, the fans are counting down to a dizzying spread of slam-bang cricket on a festive platter.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Indore | Silver Rate in Indore | Bank Holidays in Indore | Public Holidays in Indore | Petrol Price in Indore | Diesel Price in Indore | CNG Price in Indore | LPG Price in IndoreStay updated with the latest Indore news. articles.title: Smriti Mandhana replaces Harmanpreet Kaur as India captain: ‘Very special honour’
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Smriti Mandhana has been appointed the new captain of the Indian women’s side, taking over from Harmanpreet Kaur on a day of significant
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Smriti Mandhana has been appointed the new captain of the Indian women’s side, taking over from Harmanpreet Kaur on a day of significant leadership change in Indian women’s cricket.The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) announced Mandhana’s appointment on Tuesday, hours after Harmanpreet stepped down as captain across all formats. Harmanpreet, who led India to their historic maiden Women’s Cricket World Cup title in 2025 and most recently guided the side to Asian Games gold in Nagoya, will continue to represent India as a player.Mandhana, who has been part of the Indian side since 2013, will take charge as the full-time India captain. She has already led India in 18 T20Is and four ODIs and now assumes the responsibility of guiding the side into a new phase.Mandhana takes over after HarmanpreetThe change comes after Harmanpreet announced her decision to relinquish the captaincy earlier on Tuesday, bringing an end to a leadership stint that began with her taking charge of the T20I side in 2016 before becoming the full-time ODI and Test captain in 2022.Her tenure included several landmark achievements, most notably India's first Women's Cricket World Cup triumph in 2025. Harmanpreet also led India to two Asian Games gold medals, including the latest in Nagoya, and became the most-capped player in women's international cricket this year.Mandhana acknowledged the contribution of her predecessor after being handed the leadership role.“To be given the responsibility of leading India is a very special honour. Representing India has always meant a great deal to me, and to now have the opportunity to lead the team is something I will value deeply,” Mandhana said.“I would also like to acknowledge Harmanpreet and the contribution she has made as captain over the years. She has led the team with great commitment and has been an important part of our journey.”RCB success adds to Mandhana's leadership credentialsMandhana brings considerable experience into the role, both internationally and in franchise cricket. The left-hander has also captained Royal Challengers Bengaluru to two Women's Premier League titles, in 2024 and 2026.The BCCI highlighted that leadership experience while backing her to take Indian women's cricket forward.“I congratulate Smriti on being entrusted with the responsibility of leading the Indian Women’s Cricket Team,” BCCI president Mithun Manhas said.“She has been an important part of Indian cricket for many years and has consistently shown the qualities required to lead from the front. Her experience and understanding of the game will be valuable as she takes on this responsibility.”BCCI honorary secretary Devajit Saikia also pointed to Mandhana's growth as one of India's most experienced players and her success with RCB as evidence of her leadership qualities.“Leading India is a significant responsibility, but Smriti has the experience and temperament to take it on,” Saikia said.Mandhana said she understood the responsibility that comes with the new role and was ready to learn along the way.“I understand the responsibility that comes with this role and look forward to working with the team, learning along the way and giving my best to take Indian Cricket forward,” she said.Her appointment marks the beginning of a new leadership era for India, with Harmanpreet remaining part of the squad as a player while Mandhana takes over the captaincy.India women's squads for T20I and ODI series against ZimbabweIndia’s T20I Squad: Smriti Mandhana [C], Shafali Verma [VC], Niki Prasad, Harmanpreet Kaur, Anushka Sharma, Richa Ghosh [WK], G Kamalini [WK], Deepti Sharma, Prema Rawat, Sree Charani, Nandni Sharma, Kranti Gaud, Arundhati Reddy, Jintimani Kalita, Minnu ManiIndia's ODI Squad: Smriti Mandhana [C], Shafali Verma, Pratika Rawal, Harmanpreet Kaur, Harleen Deol, Tejal Hasabnis, Deepti Sharma [VC], Richa Ghosh [WK], Yastika Bhatia [WK], Vaishnavi Sharma, Nandni Sharma, Sree Charani, Kranti Gaud, Sayali Satghare, Renuka ThakurStay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: BCCI Centre of Excellence (CoE) head VVS Laxman is set to regularly attend selection meetings as the Indian cricket board aims to avoid any
articles.body: NEW DELHI: BCCI Centre of Excellence (CoE) head VVS Laxman is set to regularly attend selection meetings as the Indian cricket board aims to avoid any miscommunication between the selectors, team management and the Bengaluru facility. BCCI Secretary Devajit Saikia explained that the decision was made at the review meeting in Mumbai and will be the norm going forward.“VVS was in the meeting to ensure there is no miscommunication between the selectors and the CoE,” Saikia told TimesofIndia.com in an exclusive chat.“He is the head of cricket at the BCCI. He has all the information about the players’ injuries, so to avoid any miscommunication, Laxman should attend the selection meetings going forward. It was decided after the review meeting in Mumbai,” he further added.Saikia admitted that the continuous player injuries were a grave concern for the BCCI. When asked if the move was intended to make the selection process more transparent, Saikia said: “It is not about transparency. It is about ensuring that the selectors get complete and accurate information so that they can make the right decisions,” he said.Recently, after the third ODI against the West Indies, India captain Shubman Gill admitted that the absence of players due to multiple factors had been frustrating. He said the team does not have too much time to experiment ahead of the 2027 World Cup and wants to field the combination that is likely to play in the tournament the next time a series comes around.“I would say it’s been unfortunate, you know, with the injuries and with the scheduling, with the other matches being around. articles.body: NEW DELHI: The new leadership era in Indian women’s cricket has taken shape with Shafali Verma and Deepti Sharma appointed vice-captains of the T20I and ODI sides respectively, joining newly-appointed captain Smriti Mandhana at the helm.The changes were announced on Tuesday after Harmanpreet Kaur stepped down as India captain across formats. Harmanpreet, who will continue her international career as a player, has been retained in both squads for the upcoming home series against Zimbabwe.Shafali will serve as Mandhana’s deputy in T20Is, while Deepti has been handed the vice-captaincy in ODIs. The move gives two experienced players greater leadership responsibilities as Team India enters a new phase following Harmanpreet’s decision.Shafali, Deepti take on new rolesShafali’s elevation comes after she returned to India’s T20I setup, while Deepti remains one of the side’s most experienced all-rounders and will now support Mandhana in the 50-over format.Mandhana was appointed full-time captain earlier on Tuesday after Harmanpreet decided to relinquish the role. The 30-year-old has previously led India in 18 T20Is and four ODIs and has also enjoyed success as captain of Royal Challengers Bengaluru, guiding them to Women’s Premier League titles in 2024 and 2026.“Being given the responsibility of leading India is a very special honour. Representing India has always meant a great deal to me, and to now have the opportunity to lead the team is something I will value deeply,” Mandhana said in a BCCI release.She also acknowledged Harmanpreet’s contribution as captain.“I would also like to acknowledge Harmanpreet and the contribution she has made as captain over the years. She has led the team with great commitment and has been an important part of our journey,” she said.Zimbabwe series marks new chapterIndia’s new leadership group will begin its next assignment against Zimbabwe at home. The three-match T20I series will be played in Raipur on October 16, 18 and 20, followed by three ODIs in Vadodara on October 23, 25 and 28.The T20I squad sees Pratika Rawal left out, with Niki Prasad, Minnu Mani, Anushka Sharma and Jintimani Kalita coming into the side. All four featured in India’s recent assignments against Australia.In the ODI squad, Pratika Rawal and Harleen Deol have been included, while Jemimah Rodrigues remains unavailable after a hamstring injury. Vaishnavi Sharma, who recently claimed a six-wicket haul against Australia Women’s A, has also been named.India Squads for Zimbabwe seriesFor T20Is: Smriti Mandhana (c), Shafali Verma (vc), Niki Prasad, Harmanpreet Kaur, Anushka Sharma, Richa Ghosh (wk), G Kamalini (wk), Deepti Sharma, Prema Rawat, Sree Charani, Nandani Sharma, Kranti Gaud, Arundhati Reddy, Jintimani Kalita, Minnu Mani.For ODIs: Smriti Mandhana (c), Shafali Verma, Pratika Rawal, Harmanpreet Kaur, Harleen Deol, Tejal Hasabnis, Deepti Sharma (vc), Richa Ghosh (wk), Yastika Bhatia (wk), Vaishnavi Sharma, Nandani Sharma, Sree Charani, Kranti Gaud, Sayali Satghare, Renuka Thakur.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Shreyas Iyer's maiden T20I century powers India to eight-wicket win over West Indies
articles.summary: India skipper Shreyas Iyer marked his return to form in spectacular fashion, smashing his maiden T20I century as India cruised to an eight-wicket win over
articles.body: India skipper Shreyas Iyer marked his return to form in spectacular fashion, smashing his maiden T20I century as India cruised to an eight-wicket win over West Indies in the opening match of the five-match series on Tuesday.Chasing 172, India raced to 172 for two in just 14.4 overs, with Iyer producing a breathtaking unbeaten 102 off 43 balls. The century, completed with a towering six off Roston Chase, was the fastest by an Indian batter against West Indies in T20Is.Iyer walked off to a standing ovation after taking his helmet off and raising both hands towards the Indian dugout. His innings featured six sixes and a total of 10 boundaries.The chase did not begin without a scare. Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma added 15 runs in the opening over, but West Indies hit back through their spin duo of Akeal Hosein and Roston Chase, who dismissed both openers.Iyer took charge alongside Ishan Kishan and turned the chase into a one-sided contest. The Indian skipper's assault ensured the hosts never allowed the required rate to become a concern.Naman Dhir stars on debutEarlier, debutant Naman Dhir delivered an impressive all-round performance with the ball, claiming three wickets as India bowled West Indies out for 171 in 19.1 overs.Shai Hope top-scored for the visitors with a 37-ball 52, while Sherfane Rutherford provided the late impetus with a powerful 56 off 34 balls. West Indies made a brisk start, with Hope smashing Mayank Yadav for four boundaries in the second over. articles.title: Change of guard in Indian women’s cricket: Smriti Mandhana replaces Harmanpreet Kaur as captain
articles.summary: Mumbai: A change of guard formally took place in Indian women’s cricket on Tuesday as Harmanpreet Kaur, 37, stepped down as captain across all three
articles.body: Mumbai: A change of guard formally took place in Indian women’s cricket on Tuesday as Harmanpreet Kaur, 37, stepped down as captain across all three formats and was replaced by Smriti Mandhana, 30.Harmanpreet, who captained India to its first women’s global title in the 2025 ODI World Cup and most recently led the team’s successful defence of the Asian Games gold medal, announced her decision in an emotional Instagram post. She said she would continue as a player and was “ready to play for the love of the game again”.Harmanpreet was reportedly offered the option of continuing as ODI captain but chose to give up leadership across formats. Her decision was not entirely unexpected, with pressure building over India’s T20I results and her own recent form.The Indian cricket board (BCCI) announced Mandhana as India’s new captain across formats on Tuesday evening.The announcement came a day after Harmanpreet, Mandhana, head coach Amol Muzumdar and the national selectors met BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia in Guwahati to review the women’s team’s performance since June and discuss the roadmap ahead of the inaugural Women’s Champions Trophy in India next February. They met again on Tuesday.“Today, I step down as captain of the Indian women’s cricket team across all formats. This is not an easy decision,” Harmanpreet wrote, adding, “It carries years of memories, emotions, sacrifices and moments that will stay with me for the rest of my life. I’ve given everything I had to this team and to Indian women’s cricket — my blood, my sweat, my time, and many times, a part of my own game and personal ambitions.”Harmanpreet said every decision she made as captain was driven by the team’s interests.“I leave the captaincy today with a heart full of emotions, but also with peace,” she wrote. “Because I genuinely believe my team is in a good place — a team with talent, character, belief and a future that I am incredibly excited to watch and be a part of.”New captain Mandhana, who was vice-captain under Harmanpreet, has been in prolific form in recent years and is the leading run-getter in women’s cricket across formats, with 11,066 runs in 308 matches. She also leads the run charts in women’s T20Is with 4,867 runs in 172 games.Mandhana has also captained Royal Challengers Bengaluru to two Women’s Premier League titles, in 2024 and 2026. In an interview with TOI on July 15, she had said she was “ready for the India captaincy”.“I’d like to acknowledge Harmanpreet and the contribution she has made as captain over the years. She has led the team with great commitment and has been an important part of our journey. I understand the responsibility that comes with the role,” Mandhana was quoted as saying in a BCCI statement.Harmanpreet’s captaincy came under scrutiny after India’s league-stage exit at the 2026 Women’s T20 World Cup in June, following a similar disappointment in the UAE in 2024. Her returns with the bat had also dipped — 71 runs in five matches at the 2026 Asia Cup and 59 runs in three matches at the Asian Games.India, however, responded strongly under her, winning the one-off Test against England at Lord’s in July, the Asia Cup in the UAE and defending their Asian Games gold in Japan last month. That triumph in Nisshin was Harmanpreet’s final act as captain.Harmanpreet captained India for a decade — in five Tests, 51 ODIs and 155 T20Is. She first led India in T20Is in 2012, became full-time T20I captain in 2016 and was in charge when India reached the semi-finals of the 2018 Women’s T20 World Cup and the final in 2020. She took over the ODI captaincy in 2022 after Mithali Raj moved on and became India’s all-format skipper in 2023.In ODIs, Harmanpreet won 30 of her 51 matches as captain. Her crowning moment came at the 2025 Women’s World Cup, where India mounted a dramatic turnaround and beat South Africa in the final in Navi Mumbai. Harmanpreet also took the catch that sealed the title.During her tenure, India won three Asia Cups, the 2025 ODI World Cup, two Asian Games gold medals and a Commonwealth Games silver.Former India captain Diana Edulji called Harmanpreet’s decision “a step in the right direction”.“It’s time to move on. Harman has performed well as captain. She has taken the Indian women’s cricket team to the highest level,” Edulji told TOI.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Lucknow: Shreyas Iyer silenced his critics on Tuesday by scoring an unbeaten 102 off 43 balls as India chased down a tricky 172-run target with eight wickets and 32 balls to spare in the first T20I against the West Indies here.Iyer, who was named India’s T20I captain when he made his comeback to the team after the 2026 T20 World Cup, had been going through a tough phase and a shortage of runs on the tours of England and Ireland in June.On Tuesday, however, Iyer showed why the selectors backed him after dropping 2026 T20 World Cup-winning captain Suryakumar Yadav, bringing up his hundred off just 42 balls. In his last T20 at the Ekana Stadium, Iyer had scored an unbeaten century for Punjab Kings against Lucknow Super Giants during the last edition of the IPL.Coming in at No. 4 in the fourth over after openers Abhishek Sharma and Sanju Samson fell with the scoreboard reading 35/2, Iyer took full control of the chase.He outscored Ishan Kishan, who remained unbeaten on 37 off 27 after surviving a dropped chance, in a 137-run third-wicket partnership in just 11.1 overs. Iyer hit six sixes and 10 boundaries in his brutal assault on the West Indies bowling attack.Earlier, debutant Naman Dhir made an immediate impact with his off-spin, picking up three wickets as India bowled out the West Indies for 171.Dhir finished with impressive figures of 3/31, while Kuldeep Yadav chipped in with 2/33 as India kept the West Indies batting line-up under control after an explosive start.Sent in to bat, West Indies skipper Shai Hope wasted little time getting going. Hope’s 52 off 37 balls up front and Sherfane Rutherford’s 56 off 34 at the back end took the visitors to 171.India eventually got their first breakthrough through Arshdeep Singh, who cleaned up Kamil Pooran with a full delivery. The West Indies then suffered another setback in the sixth over when Shimron Hetmyer was run out attempting a needless single.Things got worse almost immediately. Axar Patel struck in his second over, getting Rovman Powell to go for a big heave over square leg, only to find himself bowled by a pitch-up delivery.Just when the West Indies appeared to be losing their way, Rutherford changed the momentum. articles.title: Harmanpreet Kaur's captaincy: 211 matches, one World Cup and a debate that never went away
articles.summary: Harmanpreet Kaur's captaincy began with a final and ended with one.
articles.body: Harmanpreet Kaur's captaincy began with a final and ended with one.In 2012, with Mithali Raj and Jhulan Goswami unavailable, Harmanpreet was handed the captaincy as a stand-in for the T20 Asia Cup final against Pakistan. Fourteen years later, her final match in charge was another final - India's 147-run win over Sri Lanka in the Asian Games gold-medal match.In between came 211 matches as captain, 126 wins, eight title or gold-medal finishes, India's first women's ODI World Cup triumph and the most T20I captaincy appearances in international cricket.Her leadership spanned 5074 days, beginning with that stand-in appearance in 2012 and ending with Asian Games gold in 2026. She leaves with a 59.7% win rate across formats.The 37-year-old took the reins in the shortest format full-time in 2016. After Mithali Raj's departure from international cricket in 2022, Harmanpreet became India's full-time ODI and Test captain as well. She became the first captain, male or female, to reach 150 T20Is, finishing with 155.The Questions Around Harmanpreet Kaur’s CaptaincyIn February 2020, after India lost the tri-series final to Australia from a strong position, former captain Diana Edulji suggested Harmanpreet should give up the captaincy and concentrate on her natural game.A month later, after India's defeat to Australia in the 2020 T20 World Cup final, former captain Shantha Rangaswamy also questioned whether Harmanpreet should continue as T20I captain.The debate returned in 2024. India failed to reach the T20 World Cup semi-finals for the first time during Harmanpreet's tenure. Mithali Raj said that if a leadership change was going to be made, that was the time to do it.Then India won the 2025 ODI World Cup under Harmanpreet. Days after the World Cup triumph, calls for a captaincy change only intensified.With The Bat: 1,804 ODI Runs At 44One recurring question about Harmanpreet was whether captaincy was affecting her batting. Her ODI numbers as captain offer a different picture.She scored 1,804 runs in 48 ODI innings at an average of 44.00, with four hundreds and 10 fifties. Her career ODI average is 37.22, while her strike rate as captain was 89.3, compared with 77.2 in the non-captaincy sample. Her highest score as captain was 143 not out against England at Canterbury in 2022.The ball-by-ball sample also shows a clear difference based on India's result. Harmanpreet averaged 45.51 when India won and 26.69 when India lost. All four of her captaincy hundreds in the sample came in wins.Australia Remained The Biggest HurdleIndia's record against Australia under Harmanpreet was stark. They won nine of 44 matches, losing 33, tying one and having one no-result - a 20.4% win rate. In ODIs, India won only two of 15.Australia beat India in the 2020 T20 World Cup final, 2022 Commonwealth Games final and 2023 T20 World Cup semi-final.The breakthrough came in the 2025 ODI World Cup semi-final. India chased 339, the highest successful chase in women's ODIs. Harmanpreet scored 89 off 88 balls.Before that innings, her three highest scores in captaincy knockouts had all come in defeats: 56 in the 2018 Asia Cup final, 65 in the 2022 Commonwealth Games final and 52 in the 2023 T20 World Cup semi-final.The 89 against Australia was her first fifty as captain in a knockout match that India won. Four days later, India won the World Cup.Eight titles - But Not The T20 World CupHarmanpreet led India at 16 major tournaments, with three of those involving captaincy only in the final.India finished with a title or gold medal at eight of those tournaments: the 2012 and 2016 T20 Asia Cups, 2017 World Cup Qualifier, 2022 T20 Asia Cup, 2022 Asian Games, 2025 ODI World Cup, 2026 T20 Asia Cup and 2026 Asian Games.The T20 World Cup remained the missing trophy.India reached the semi-finals in 2018 and 2023, lost the final in 2020, and exited at the group stage in 2024 and 2026.The World Cup Finally Came In 2025The World Cup record under Harmanpreet had several near misses before India finally got there. India lost the 2020 T20 World Cup final under her captaincy, followed by a semi-final exit in 2023 and a group-stage exit in 2024.In 2025, India beat Australia in the semi-final, with Harmanpreet's 89 setting up the run to the final. India then beat South Africa by 52 runs to win its first women's ODI World Cup title.The victory also put Harmanpreet in a small group of Indian captains. She became only the third Indian captain, after Kapil Dev and MS Dhoni, to win the 50-over World Cup.She joined an even shorter list of Indian captains to have lifted a World Cup, alongside Kapil, Dhoni, Rohit Sharma and Suryakumar Yadav.Her World Cup knockout record as captain finished at two wins and three defeats, with two finals and one title. Both victories came in 2025.Overall, Harmanpreet captained India in 24 knockout matches and won 16. In finals, the record was nine wins and six defeats.Captaincy Milestones: A Record Book of FirstsHarmanpreet became the first captain, male or female, to reach 150 T20Is, finishing with 155 - the most in international cricket.She was also the first cricketer to reach 200 T20I appearances, while her 92 T20I wins as captain are the most by a woman.As captain, she led India to its first Test win over Australia, a record 347-run Test victory over England, and the country's first women's ODI World Cup title in 2025.Her 143 not out against England in Canterbury in 2022 remains the highest ODI score by an Indian women's captain.The 2025 World Cup semi-final produced the highest successful chase in women's ODIs, with India chasing 339 against Australia.Her final match added another record: India's 147-run win over Sri Lanka in the 2026 Asian Games final, the country's biggest T20I victory by runs.The final StretchThe final year of Harmanpreet's captaincy had two very different phases.India lost seven matches in a row between February and April 2026 - three ODIs and a Test against Australia, followed by three T20Is against South Africa. The T20 World Cup group-stage exit followed in June.India then won eight T20Is in succession, taking the Asia Cup and Asian Games gold. Her final match as captain was the Asian Games final, where India beat Sri Lanka by 147 runs.Harmanpreet stepped away after 14 years as India's captain, with the ODI World Cup, two Asian Games golds and four T20 Asia Cup titles on her record.She also leaves with the T20 World Cup still missing, a difficult record against Australia and a succession debate that continued even after the 2025 World Cup triumph.In her resignation statement on Instagram, Harmanpreet confirmed that she was stepping down as captain across all formats but would continue as a player."This is not an easy decision. It carries years of memories, emotions, sacrifices, and moments that will stay with me for the rest of my life," she said."Now, I'm ready to play for the love of the game again. Captaincy ends. The journey continues."She also said she was leaving with peace and that she felt she had "done my duty".For a captain whose tenure began with a final in 2012, it ended in the same setting 14 years later - with another trophy, another gold medal, and the captaincy finally behind her.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Greatest pile of mediocrity’: Matthew Hayden tears into Australia selectors over ‘disrespecting first-class cricket’
articles.summary: Former Australia opener Matthew Hayden has launched a strong criticism of the national selection panel over Nic Maddinson’s recall for the three-Test
articles.body: Former Australia opener Matthew Hayden has launched a strong criticism of the national selection panel over Nic Maddinson’s recall for the three-Test series against South Africa, questioning the decision to bring back a batter who has not played first-class cricket since early 2025.Maddinson, 34, was added to Australia’s squad amid a mounting injury crisis ahead of the series opener in Durban on October 9. Josh Inglis has been ruled out with a finger injury, while Cameron Green remains a doubt for the first Test.However, Hayden believes the circumstances do not justify Maddinson’s return to the Test set-up, particularly given his lack of recent first-class cricket.Speaking on the All Over Bar The Cricket podcast, the former 103-Test opener questioned whether Maddinson would be capable of making a significant impact if Australia called upon him during the series.“Where we are at is that we are promoting the greatest pile of mediocrity that we’ve seen in a generation of cricket,” Hayden said on the All Over Bar The Cricket podcast.Hayden also took aim at chief selector George Bailey and Tony Dodemaide, arguing that Australia should be selecting players with stronger first-class records rather than relying on batters with modest averages.“And if we continue to lay that out and expect that a bloke averaging 35 is going to average 55 in Test match cricket, George Bailey and Tony Dodemaide, you are dreaming. I will just put it that simply. You are frigging dreaming. And you are piling up this dog s*** explanation, and you are, in my opinion, disrespecting first-class cricket. Absolutely dead set you are. You should be picking guys that are averaging 45 or more, and you can’t, because they don’t want to play," said Hayden.Maddinson has not featured in a Test since the 2016-17 home summer, when he scored just 27 runs across three matches. His first-class average of 37.11 has further fuelled the debate around his selection.His return to the squad comes after a difficult period that included treatment for testicular cancer.Hayden questions alternative optionsHayden suggested Sam Harper could have been considered instead. The wicketkeeper-batter recently impressed on Australia A’s tour of India, where he also scored a century, before being added to the Test squad.The former opener also questioned the selection credentials of all-rounder Mitchell Marsh, pointing to his limited participation in state-level red-ball cricket.Hayden argued that Marsh’s lack of Shield cricket should matter despite Australia captain Pat Cummins backing the all-rounder.“I don’t care what Pat Cummins said about Mitch – if he doesn’t want to play Shield cricket … it’s a desire to front up,” Hayden said.He further criticised the growing preference among players for franchise cricket over domestic red-ball cricket, identifying it as a wider issue for Australian cricket.“They don’t want to play this version of the game. Mitch is a good example. He is making millions of dollars playing cricket all over the world for franchises. This is the fundamental problem we have," added Hayden.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Test cricket's biggest scandals: Your top 10 revealed
articles.summary: See what BBC Sport readers voted as Test cricket's biggest scandals, together with contributions from the TMS team.
articles.body:
On Friday, Australia will play their first Test in South Africa since the sandpapergate scandal rocked the cricketing world eight years ago.

To mark one of the biggest controversies the game has ever seen, Test Match Special asked you which is Test cricket's biggest scandal.

Ten of the most notorious scandals in Test cricket were picked out by a TMS panel and readers of the BBC Sport website then ranked them.

The results have been revealed on the TMS podcast by BBC chief cricket commentator Jonathan Agnew, former England fast bowler Steven Finn and TMS scorer Andy Zaltzman.

The full results are below and you can listen to the podcast here .

Pakistan had already lost the series in England in 2006, yet were cruising to victory in the final Test at The Oval. However, Australian umpire Darrel Hair asked for the ball to be changed midway through the afternoon session on the fourth day. Ball-tampering was suggested and Pakistan refused to play after tea. The match was abandoned and years later awarded to England, after some back and forth.

Agnew: "Pakistan weren't accused of ball-tampering, they were found guilty of ball-tampering, on the field, without any opportunity to defend themselves. The rule at the time was if the umpire on the field suspected ball-tampering, the ball was changed and penalty runs were awarded. It didn't feel fair."

Zaltzman: "It ended up with England awarded the Test so therefore they won the series 3-0. It means that whenever we look at the biggest first-innings deficit overturned to win a Test, this game comes out on top - 331 runs. It irritates me slightly."

England's Test match against Pakistan in 1987 was stopped mid-game for more than 24 hours when the tourists' skipper Mike Gatting became embroiled in a row with home umpire Shakoor Rana.

Agnew: "I'm a bit surprised this is so low. The knock-on was England didn't tour Pakistan for many years. England felt they were being stitched up by Pakistani umpires. There was a total lack of trust, going both ways, between England and Pakistan for a very long time."

Zaltzman : "This was before neutral umpires and there was a sense umpiring wasn't quite as fair as it could have been, which all exploded in that moment."

Finn: "It blows my mind that there weren't neutral umpires. My first summer of Test cricket had DRS and neutral umpires."

The third Test in the 1975 Ashes was abandoned when the pitch was vandalised overnight by supporters of George Davis, who had been jailed for armed robbery the previous year. "George Davis is innocent" was written on the wall around Headingley.

Finn: "I can't fathom turning up to a Test match and the pitch - the most sacred, untouchable of places - it's staggering that people managed to do that."

Zaltzman: "It highlights how vulnerable cricket is to this sort of thing. A small bit of the field is damaged and the whole game has to be abandoned."

Agnew: "There was no security. These days, the grounds are locked down. It was set up for an England win, but could have been a really good game of cricket. It's a bizarre story."

When Australia's richest man, Kerry Packer, failed to boost the ratings of his Channel Nine TV network with live cricket, he created his own product: World Series Cricket. The plan was simple - Packer recruited the best players in the world to stage his own matches.

Agnew: "Virtually everything you see about modern cricket can be traced back to World Series. It was incredible, innovative and exciting. I was 18 years old, playing club cricket in Melbourne and captivated by the coverage."

Finn: "There's a similar revolution going on at the moment with T20 leagues allowing players to drift away from Test cricket. The temptation to be involved in something new and exciting would have been very interesting."

Zaltzman: "It was extremely high-calibre cricket, but not even counted in first-class statistics, let alone Test stats. I don't really see it as a scandal at all, it was more cricket growing up. This really modernised the sport."

In the 1994 Lord's Test against South Africa, Michael Atherton was caught by TV cameras rubbing dirt on the ball. Atherton's explanation was that he was trying to maintain the condition of the ball, rather than alter it. Trouble was, he told the match referee he was using the dirt to keep his hands dry.

Agnew: "This was a really tough time. I've thought about this a lot over the years and I'm not sure Michael knew the rules at the time - cricketers often don't. It's OK to rub your hand in the dirt, but you can't put soil on to the ball. It was a huge story. It was everywhere."

Our top five kicks off with the Pakistan spot-fixing scandal of 2010, when no-balls deliberately bowled in the Lord's Test ultimately resulted in three of the tourists' players - team captain Salman Butt and fast bowlers Mohammad Asif and Mohammad Amir - spending time in jail.

Finn: "This was my first summer of Test cricket. It was such a weird atmosphere. We were warming up, looked up to the Pakistan dressing room and there were two officials in suits and blazers reading the News of the World. That was the day we went on to win the game. We didn't celebrate any of the wickets because of what transpired."

Zaltzman: "Amir had burst on to the scene as a teenager - he'd only bowled three no-balls in his previous five Tests. As a cricket fan, one of the deep sadnesses was Amir was one of the best talents to have emerged in years. It was an individual tragedy. A young player had been led astray."

The Australians feature again here, but this time the guilty party was England, who developed a plan of intimidatory fast bowling aimed at the bodies of the hosts' batters in the 1932-33 Ashes series.

Agnew: "For me, this would be bottom. It was an entirely legitimate ploy. They call us whingeing Poms, but the Australians were pretty good at whingeing about the way [Harold] Larwood was bowling."

Finn: "Cricket is a game of small margins. You use the laws and the bandwidth within those laws. Play on, I say."

The most recent of the scandals in our list is Sandpapergate, when Australia's cricketers were found to have used sandpaper to alter the condition of the ball during their Test match against South Africa in Cape Town.

Finn: "I was completely and utterly baffled and shocked that someone thought this was a good idea and they would get away with it. There are so many cameras and you are so acutely aware when you are playing that those cameras have the ability to zoom in. To think you'd be able to pull sandpaper out of your pocket, rub it on the ball and then hide it down your pants is completely unfathomable. I was shocked they had taken altering the state of the ball to that kind of level."

Agnew: "If you're a bowler you want to control what's happening with the ball and you'll see if something has gone on with it. For me, there are some unanswered questions. It was one of the most stupid things ever seen on a cricket field."

A close second in our vote was the Basil D'Oliveira affair of 1968, when England's tour of South Africa was called off over the inclusion in their squad of mixed-race all-rounder D'Oliveira. At the time, South Africa was operating under a system of racial segregation known as apartheid.

Agnew: "You can actually trace this affair all the way up to the birth of a new nation. When you unpick it, look at the consequences, it was eventually the birth of a new South Africa. For me, this would be number one."

Zaltzman: "There's still a lot that is not known about the decision to not pick D'Oliveira in the original England squad. There had been pressure put on him by the English cricketing establishment - the establishment came out very badly from that. It had a huge impact on the world and the gradual dismantling of apartheid."

Top of the list is former South Africa captain Hansie Cronje, who admitted to match-fixing having become involved with Indian bookmakers. Cronje's most infamous plot came in a dead-rubber fifth Test against England at Centurion Park in 2000. The match had been badly affected by rain, but Cronje was adamant the teams should do all they could to ensure it did not end in a draw.

He negotiated with England skipper Nasser Hussain for both teams to forfeit an innings, leaving the tourists with a final-day run-chase, which they completed. England were unaware, but Cronje had engineered a result.

Agnew: "This was unbelievable. It came to light by accident. The Delhi police were trying to tap a phone of a bookmaker and accidentally tapped the phone of Hansie Cronje. Thank goodness they did because hopefully it is now much more difficult for a player to manipulate games of cricket."

Zaltzman: "At the time, we all thought it was good. Cronje's generous deal made a contest on the final day of a dead rubber. Until the true story came out, we didn't realise what had gone was criminal. The shock of the story merits its place in this countdown."

Finn: "A lot of these things have been the catalyst for necessary change in cricket and this was the biggest one."

articles.title: Ethan Bamber for England? Should Warwickshire seamer be considered for spot in Test cricket bowling attack?
articles.summary: Ethan Bamber took 69 wickets at an average below 20 as Warwickshire won the County Championship in 2026; Michael Atherton says of Bamber: "He's somebody who wants to get absolutely the most out of every little bit of talent he's got"; Chris Woakes calls Jofra Archer leader of Test attack
articles.body:
The Warwickshire star, 27, was the leading County Championship wicket-taker in the country in 2026, with his 69 scalps at an average of 19.39 helping the Bears to the Division One title.

Bamber is an Ollie Robinson figure as opposed to a Jofra Archer one, relying on skill and nagging accuracy rather than pace and hostility.

But with it now in vogue for wicketkeepers to stand up close to the stumps to seamers wobbling the ball, perhaps Bamber has a chance of a maiden international call-up?

Bamber for England? 'Never say never...'

Sky Sports' Michael Atherton said on the England prospects of the former Middlesex man, who has 308 scalps in 89 first-class matches at an average below 27: "A few years ago, you'd have said no - a bowler of 78, 80 miles an hour, wobbling it about.

"But now everybody's keen on the wobble seam and the wicketkeeper standing up. So never say never. I wouldn't imagine so but I see him as a very, very good county bowler.

"England have got Ollie Robinson there at the moment and they'll always have one of those fellas in the mix, won't they?

"Whether it's Robinson or Sam Cook, who seems to be kind of Robinson's understudy at the moment, so you could see Bamber maybe in that role.

"He's a cracking kid and somebody who wants to get absolutely the most out of every little bit of talent that he's got.

"He moved to Warwickshire with ambitions to go to a club that's challenging for things and is making the most of what he's got."

Bamber brushed off the likelihood of international honours while speaking to Cricinfo at the recent Professional Cricketers' Association awards in London, saying: "If that ship was ever in the harbour, it's definitely sailed now.

"What I'm thinking of is how I can contribute next year for Warwickshire, and try to help us continue to be successful moving forward. That's really what makes me a bit nervous and excited."

'Archer at peak of his powers - now the leader of the attack'

England's attack starred during the 3-0 rout of Pakistan this summer, with Robinson bagging 21 wickets at an average below nine and Archer 12 at 26.66.

Gus Atkinson and Josh Tongue also played their part, while Cook, Sonny Baker and Matthew Fisher are back-up options.

The quicks will return to red-ball cricket from December 17, live on Sky Sports , for a three-Test series in South Africa - Stephen Fleming's first assignment as head coach.

Former England seamer Chris Woakes, speaking at the launch of the ECB's 'Cricket for Teachers' initiative , told Sky Sports News : "The bowling attack looks great, plenty of depth.

"Robinson has come back in and done fantastically well - South Africa will be a different challenge but he has the skills to succeed.

"The beauty of Jofra is that he has played a lot of cricket over the last few years and stayed injury-free - he looks as fit as ever and is kind of the leader of the attack now.

"He has matured a lot as a bowler and a person. He is at the peak of his powers and wants to be playing his best Test cricket.

articles.summary: India head coach Gautam Gambhir bid farewell to outgoing chief selector Ajit Agarkar, praising his conviction and highlighting the three ICC trophies
articles.body: India head coach Gautam Gambhir bid farewell to outgoing chief selector Ajit Agarkar, praising his conviction and highlighting the three ICC trophies India won during his tenure.“Dear Ajit Bhai, an absolute honour to work with you. Those 3 ICC trophies are testimony of your conviction: Team first & Team ahead, always.. I must say, History will be kinder to you. Thank you for everything. My heartfelt wishes for your future endeavours,” Gambhir posted on X.Agarkar’s tenure as chairman of the senior men’s selection committee officially ended on Tuesday, with the BCCI inviting applications to fill the vacant position.The former India pacer took charge in July 2023 and completed his term on October 4. He had informed the BCCI after its Annual General Meeting on September 18 that he would not seek an extension.During Agarkar’s stint, India reached the 2023 ODI World Cup final before winning the 2024 T20 World Cup, the 2025 Champions Trophy and the 2026 T20 World Cup.Gambhir, who worked closely with Agarkar during his tenure as India head coach, acknowledged the selector’s approach of putting the team ahead of individual considerations.Ojha takes interim chargeFormer India spinner Pragyan Ojha is currently serving as interim chairman of selectors and chaired the meeting that picked India’s squad for the upcoming New Zealand tour.Ojha, who played 24 Tests for India, could be appointed the full-time chairman based on seniority if the BCCI’s eventual choice has played fewer Tests.Parthiv Patel, whose name has emerged as a possible addition to the selection panel, would have greater seniority than Ojha, having played 25 Tests for India.The BCCI has invited applications for one position on the five-member senior men’s selection committee. articles.title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has conquered the hype. Now comes the hard part: Waiting
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: One will have to feel for 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: One will have to feel for 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi.Whenever VVS Laxman has been at the helm, Sooryavanshi has played for India, be it in Zimbabwe or at the recently concluded 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. To accommodate the teenager in the playing XI, Sanju Samson moved down to No. 3. But with Gautam Gambhir back for the West Indies T20I series, Sooryavanshi has been left warming the bench.The youngster did make his India debut under Gambhir during the tour of England earlier this year, but India's head coach made it clear that Sooryavanshi will have to wait for his opportunity. Gambhir has also made no secret of his faith in Samson, India's Player of the Tournament in the 2026 T20 World Cup. He admitted that leaving the Kerala batter out during India's tour of England was the "toughest decision" he has made since taking charge as head coach.In the first T20I against West Indies, Sooryavanshi was again on the bench, with Samson opening alongside Abhishek Sharma. Samson's stay at the crease lasted only nine balls before he hit a half-tracker straight back to Akeal Hosein. It was a soft dismissal, and in the commentary box, Ian Bishop, one of Samson's many admirers, could not help but question the batter's consistency.The world sees him differently, and he sees himself differently in the world. What is in his control is the only thing that we can talk about: how he manages himself in this new world that he is in and how he manages the way the world responds to the new Sooryavanshi.The question, then, is where does that leave Sooryavanshi?Sujith Somasunder, former India and Karnataka opener and a sports psychologist, believes the teenager now has to learn how to navigate a world that has changed dramatically since his emergence as one of Indian cricket's biggest young stars.“Sooryavanshi has achieved what he has achieved so far on his own. Now, suddenly, his status in the cricketing world has moved to a different tangent. The world sees him differently, and he sees himself differently in the world. What is in his control is the only thing that we can talk about: how he manages himself in this new world that he is in and how he manages the way the world responds to the new Sooryavanshi. That is a very important aspect of how he will be able to control and manage this situation,” Somasunder told TimesofIndia.com.“Sooryavanshi has to realise that, ‘I am now going to get into the water, so I need to know how to swim.’ Similarly, he needs to understand that the world I am in now is a little different from what it was before I became Sooryavanshi. He will also need to learn and understand how to navigate this situation for himself,” he added.Sooryavanshi is now fighting for a place in the playing XI with Samson, the man whose 97 not out, 89 and 89 in the knockout stages helped India defend their T20 World Cup title. But since those heroics, Samson has managed only two half-centuries in 11 innings, both coming in Delhi, a venue traditionally favourable to batters. In six of those innings, he has been dismissed for single-digit scores.Sooryavanshi, meanwhile, is still only 15. He has already become a superstar, despite being at the very beginning of his international career. He endured a difficult start against Jofra Archer and Co. in England, but found his groove in Zimbabwe and looked in excellent touch at the Asian Games.Someone doesn't become a Player of the Tournament in a World Cup without having the talent. So Sanju Samson has done enough.Yet Gambhir has drawn a clear line for now. Unless Samson's lean run continues, Sooryavanshi could have to wait longer than expected for another opportunity.Gambhir, however, has stressed that Samson does not need anyone to validate his place in the team, pointing to his performances as proof of his ability.“First of all, he doesn't need to give me any credit (for proper communication when he wasn't playing). His talent itself is enough for him to be in the dressing room. He's shown what he's capable of. Someone doesn't become a Player of the Tournament in a World Cup without having the talent. So he's done enough,” Gambhir said in an interview with Jio Hotstar, praising Samson.“From Vaibhav's point of view, it was again a very clear conversation that he has to wait for his opportunity. We know the kind of talent he has. We know what he can do,” Gambhir had said about Sooryavanshi.For Somasunder, though, the waiting period is not necessarily a setback. It could be an important part of Sooryavanshi's development, provided the teenager is given the right support and guidance.He gives the example of Australia and Ricky Ponting, a prodigiously talented youngster who was identified early as a potential future leader.“In the world of cricket, the way it has gone in India, the onus is always on the individual. In Australia, for example, I remember Ricky Ponting was a very brash young talent. I have heard, though I am not sure if it is true and I have not verified it, that the Australian Institute of Sport, as it was called initially, identified Ricky Ponting as a leader. What they did was take the initiative to groom Ponting as the next captain. He was a very brash young kid, but if they saw that he could be the future captain of the Australian team, then they needed to groom him to behave appropriately and develop the right leadership skills,” he said.Somasunder believes Indian cricket could similarly look beyond simply managing Sooryavanshi's performances and invest in preparing him for the pressures that come with being one of the country's most talked-about young cricketers.“Meanwhile, in our culture, which is relationship-oriented, Australia could be described as more task-oriented. So there are certain nuances to a relationship-oriented culture when it comes to individuals. In a task-oriented culture, there is more individualism. In a hierarchical culture, people tend to bow down to someone higher in the hierarchy. In an individualistic culture, everybody will call themselves by their own name and might even call the coach by his first name,” he added.For Sooryavanshi, this may be his first real lesson in the less glamorous side of international cricket. He has already learnt how to announce himself on the biggest stage. Now, he must learn how to wait for it. articles.title: ‘My reputation has been tarnished’: Ash Gardner opens up on affair and marriage breakdown
articles.summary: Ash Gardner has spoken publicly for the first time about the alleged affair with teammate Georgia Voll that contributed to the breakdown of her marriage
articles.body: Ash Gardner has spoken publicly for the first time about the alleged affair with teammate Georgia Voll that contributed to the breakdown of her marriage to Monica Wright.Gardner said the situation became far more public than she expected and admitted she had been “naive” about the level of attention it would attract.The controversy came to light earlier this year when Wright revealed the affair on social media. The relationship is believed to have begun during the Women’s World Cup in India last year. Gardner has since apologised to Wright and said she has spent time reflecting on what happened.Gardner reflects on public falloutSpeaking to Australian outlet CODE Sports, Gardner acknowledged that her public image had taken a hit, saying, “My reputation has been tarnished with the public, but I guess something that I always try to strive to do when representing any team that I play in is be the best teammate that I can, and hopefully show what this team means to me when I’m playing for them.”The Australian vice-captain also said being a high-profile athlete means personal matters can attract intense public interest.“Playing sport at a high level, you’re open to having a platform, and sometimes with this comes interest from the public, and they want to know things about your personal life, and they invest, and then can make judgment either way of what you are or aren’t doing.”Gardner wants to move forwardGardner admitted she was shocked when Wright publicly identified Voll, writing, “This is who my wife cheated on me with,” alongside a photo of the teammate.“I was certainly surprised, as you could imagine,” Gardner said.She added, “I certainly didn’t expect the situation to take the path that it did, or to become as public as what it did. But I also understand that everyone has their own way of dealing with difficult situations.”Gardner said she now wants to focus on learning from the experience, having difficult conversations where necessary and moving forward with the Australian team.She also said she understood Wright’s perspective and tried to remain positive during what she described as a very difficult period.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘When are you going to play him?’: Ex-India batter questions  decision to bench Nitish Reddy
articles.summary: Former India opener Aakash Chopra believes the team management’s selection thinking does not currently match his own, questioning the decision to leave
articles.body: Former India opener Aakash Chopra believes the team management’s selection thinking does not currently match his own, questioning the decision to leave out Nitish Kumar Reddy from the first T20I against the West Indies in Lucknow.India began the five-match series with an eight-wicket win on Tuesday after bowling out the West Indies for 171 and chasing down the target with 32 balls to spare.While Chopra felt Reddy should have featured in the series opener, he also praised Naman Dhir for making a strong impact after being trusted with the ball.“The spinners took eight (seven) wickets. Personally, I would put my hand up. I thought Nitish Kumar Reddy should have been played. If you are not going to play Nitish now, when are you going to play him? My thinking and the Indian team's alignment are not sitting together,” he said in a video shared on his YouTube channel, 'Aakash Chopra.'Dhir justified the faith shown in him by returning figures of 3/31 from his four overs. His three wickets came immediately after he had been hit for a six, with Shai Hope, Romario Shepherd and Shamar Springer all dismissed following maximums off the previous delivery.Chopra was particularly impressed by the way Dhir adjusted his bowling and responded to the pressure.“However, there is one thing for sure. This team has great confidence in Naman Dhir. They feel this guy has a huge upside, which is correct. He bats very well, and they are repeatedly making him bowl along with that. Only five bowlers were used, and he picked up three wickets, where he also applied his brain,” the cricketer-turned-commentator observed.“He got hit for a six and bowled the next ball slightly far and slow. Then he bowled a slightly flat and full ball to Romario Shepherd on his legs and got hit for a six. He got the next ball to drift away with a round arm. That tells you that the guy is thinking and is executing that skill after that. The seam position was good. So, a lot of things were super impressive about Naman Dhir,” he added.Dhir removed Hope after the West Indies batter made 52 off 37 balls, before dismissing Shepherd for 7 off 5 and Springer for 9 off 7.Chopra unhappy with West Indies battingChopra also criticised the West Indies for failing to make the most of the conditions, arguing that the hosts should have been chasing a much higher total.He praised Kuldeep Yadav, who took 2/33 in four overs, and Axar Patel, who returned 2/26 from 3.1 overs, but felt the West Indies batting unit failed to capitalise.“Kuldeep Yadav picked up two wickets. Axar Patel bowled the sixth over as a maiden and picked up Rovman Powell's wicket in that. West Indies, you didn't bat well. This was a pitch on which 200 should have been scored easily. Your batting was extremely ordinary, and you reached 170,” he said.Shai Hope and Sherfane Rutherford were the only West Indies batters to make substantial contributions, with Hope scoring 52 and Rutherford hitting 56 off 34 balls.Chopra also pointed to Mayank Yadav's performance as an area of concern. The fast bowler, returning from injury, finished with 1/40 from his four overs and appeared to rely heavily on slower deliveries.“You left a lot on the pitch. Hope scored a fifty and another fifty by Sherfane Rutherford, but what happened in the middle was avoidable. Mayank Yadav was slightly expensive. It felt like he was slightly rusty, as he is returning from injury and hasn't played a lot of cricket,” Chopra observed.Only Akeal Hosein, who made 15 off 9, and Kamil Pooran, with 12 off 11, joined Hope and Rutherford in reaching double figures for the West Indies.India's bowlers ultimately kept the visitors to 171 before Shreyas Iyer's unbeaten 102 off 43 balls powered the hosts to a comfortable victory and a 1-0 series lead.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Game-changing approach’: ACB chief hails ILT20 management after 25 Afghan players earn contracts
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Afghanistan Cricket Board chief executive Naseeb Khan Zadran has heaped praise on the ILT20 management for its “game-changing approach” towards
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Afghanistan Cricket Board chief executive Naseeb Khan Zadran has heaped praise on the ILT20 management for its “game-changing approach” towards Afghanistan cricket after 25 Afghan players secured contracts across the league’s six franchises for Season 5.Zadran described the partnership between the ACB, Emirates Cricket Board and ILT20 as an “incredible start” and specifically credited ILT20 chairman Khalid Al Zarooni and league commissioner Mubashshir Usmani for helping create greater opportunities for Afghan cricketers.“Mr. Zarooni and Mr. Mubashshir’s vision for the growth of the game is truly inspirational, which is proven by the ILT20’s game-changing approach for both Associate Members and Full Members like Afghanistan,” Zadran said.The ACB has secured the participation of 25 Afghan players across the six franchise squads through its strategic alliance with the ECB. Under the agreement between the two boards, each franchise must include at least four Afghan players in its squad, while the Season 5 playing conditions require a minimum of two Afghan players in every playing XI.The provisions have created defined opportunities for Afghan cricketers at both squad and match level, with established internationals and emerging players set to feature in the UAE-based competition.The auction attracted strong interest in Afghan players, with Fazalhaq Farooqi and Rahmanullah Gurbaz among the leading signings. Zadran said the two had earned “record amounts of money” through the bidding.“The auction has raised the profile of Afghanistan cricket and players like never before. A total of 25 Afghanistan players have earned contracts with the DP World ILT20 franchises, with Fazalhaq Farooqi and Rahmanullah Gurbaz earning record amounts of money through their massive bidding amounts,” he said.Zadran also credited the partnership with the ILT20 and ECB for providing a professional pathway for Afghan players and helping expand the game in the country.“This opportunity for our players is a result of our incredible partnership with the DP World ILT20 and the Emirates Cricket Board,” he said. “We reached a strategic decision with them earlier this year with an aim of further expanding the game in Afghanistan through the ILT20/ECB’s support.”He also singled out Al Zarooni and Usmani for their role in implementing the partnership.“I want to take this opportunity to thank the Chairman ILT20 Khalid Al Zarooni and League Commissioner Mubashshir Usmani, who were instrumental in the implementation and execution of this partnership,” Zadran said.Zadran added that the ACB was confident the partnership would continue to benefit Afghan cricket.“We are off to an incredible start in our partnership, and we have full confidence that this partnership will continue to support our players and inspire a new generation of Afghanistan stars,” he said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: SA20 auction 2026: Who has the biggest purse and what each team needs - everything you need to know
articles.summary: The SA20 Season 5 Player Auction will take place on Wednesday, with four franchises set to fill 19 remaining slots and a combined $2.10 million available
articles.body: The SA20 Season 5 Player Auction will take place on Wednesday, with four franchises set to fill 19 remaining slots and a combined $2.10 million available to spend.Durban’s Super Giants and Paarl Royals have already completed their squad-building after the league increased the salary cap to $2.54 million for the upcoming season.Among the four teams heading into the auction, Joburg Super Kings have the biggest purse with $1.245 million available. MI Cape Town have $565,150, Sunrisers Eastern Cape have $217,600, while Pretoria Capitals have just $89,150 remaining.Joburg Super Kings and MI Cape Town must each sign one Under-23 player from the final shortlist of 48 players. Joburg also have a wildcard slot still available.There will be no Right to Match cards at the Season 5 auction.How the squads will be completedEach team must have 19 players in its registered squad, comprising 18 regular squad members and one wildcard player.The 18-player squad can have a maximum of seven overseas players and must include at least 11 South African players, with two of those required to be Under-23 players.The wildcard can be either a South African or overseas player and will not count towards the salary cap.The auction will feature marquee mixed-set rounds followed by a nomination express round, in which teams can call up the player they want to bid for.The auction takes place on October 7, with SA20 Season 5 following a previous edition in which Dewald Brevis became the league's most expensive player after Pretoria Capitals bought him for R16.5 million.Matthew Breetzke is another player whose auction value has risen significantly. Durban’s Super Giants initially signed him for his base price of $10,576 at the inaugural auction before Sunrisers Eastern Cape bought him for $368,000 three seasons later.SA20 auction 2026: Time and where to watchThe Season 5 Player Auction begins at 8:30pm IST on Wednesday, October 7.In India, the auction will be broadcast on JioHotstar.
